book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Harry Potter: An eleven-year-old orphan who has grown up in a cupboard discovers that strangers know his name. His instinct is to side with the person being picked on.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Hermione Granger: A Muggle-born student arriving at Hogwarts exceptionally well prepared. Her determination to get the answer right masks a newcomer's anxiety about belonging.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Ron Weasley: The youngest Weasley son at Hogwarts has inherited robes, family stories and several reputations to live up to. At chess he gets to make the decisions.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Rubeus Hagrid: Hogwarts's enormous gamekeeper welcomes creatures that other people prudently avoid. Tenderness and an unfortunate inability to keep a secret make him Harry's first real friend.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Albus Dumbledore: The headmaster can put a nervous child at ease with an absurd remark. His apparent distraction rarely prevents him from noticing what matters.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Quirinus Quirrell: The nervous Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher stammers through encounters with colleagues. His account of travelling abroad makes him a subject of school gossip.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Severus Snape: The Potions master speaks softly enough to make a classroom lean forward. Harry finds that the man already has strong feelings about a boy he barely knows.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Draco Malfoy: A wealthy first-year boy who arrives certain he knows which wizarding families matter. He expects other children to organize themselves around the same hierarchy.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Minerva McGonagall: The Transfiguration professor demands precision and enforces school rules without fuss. Her fierce interest in Gryffindor Quidditch occasionally produces a surprising exception.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Neville Longbottom: A forgetful boy raised by a formidable grandmother. It takes him time to recognize the courage involved in standing up to people he likes.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Lord Voldemort (Tom Riddle): The dark wizard whose attack left Harry orphaned and scarred. Even his name can make an otherwise talkative room fall silent.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Vernon Dursley: Harry's uncle sells drills and prizes normality. Faced with something inexplicable, he generally tries shouting, shutting a door or driving away.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Petunia Dursley: Harry's aunt takes pride in a spotless suburban home. Any reminder of her magical sister threatens the life she has built around being conventional.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Dudley Dursley: The Dursleys' indulged son is accustomed to extra presents, a plentiful breakfast and a cousin who takes the blame.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Oliver Wood: Gryffindor's Keeper and Quidditch captain explains tactics with evangelical urgency. Finding a gifted Seeker matters considerably more to him than the Seeker's age.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Fred Weasley: One of Ron's older twin brothers, a Gryffindor Beater with a gift for turning family familiarity into a perfectly timed provocation.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.George Weasley: Fred's twin and fellow Beater knows when to complete a joke and when to let Fred's line hang. Their partnership includes looking out for younger students.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Percy Weasley: Ron's prefect brother takes rules and the badge that goes with them seriously. His siblings have ample opportunity to test his dignity.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Firenze: A centaur in the Forbidden Forest who judges a child's immediate danger more pressing than his herd's customary distance from human affairs.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Peeves: Hogwarts's resident poltergeist invents insulting songs, disrupts corridors and treats an audience of furious adults as an invitation to encore.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Griphook: A goblin at Gringotts guides Harry through its underground vaults. His professional manner hints at a wizarding institution with its own traditions and loyalties.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Garrick Ollivander: The wandmaker remembers the properties of wands he sold decades ago. Fitting Harry is an experiment whose outcome interests him rather intensely.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Madam Hooch: The flying instructor expects first-years to listen before they mount a broom. A sharp eye and a whistle help maintain order on the pitch.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Lee Jordan: A friend of the Weasley twins whose Quidditch commentary is lively, partisan and frequently subject to intervention by Professor McGonagall.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ph.Seamus Finnigan: An Irish Gryffindor in Harry's year whose upbringing bridges magical and Muggle households. Dormitory conversation gives his classmates their first introduction to that history.

book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Katniss Everdeen: A District 12 hunter who volunteers for her little sister. She reads tracks and faces expertly until someone asks her to interpret an act of affection.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Peeta Mellark: A baker's son whose skill with icing translates unexpectedly well to camouflage. He understands what an audience wants to hear and worries about what performing will cost him.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Haymitch Abernathy: District 12's surviving victor drinks heavily and notices everything. His abrasive coaching makes more sense once you understand whom the Games are designed to please.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Gale Hawthorne: Katniss's hunting partner sets ingenious snares. He shares her duty to feed a family and has a much greater appetite for open rebellion.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Rue: A young District 11 tribute who can slip through a tree canopy and communicate by birdsong. Watching from above has taught her a great deal about other people.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Effie Trinket: The Capitol escort for District 12 believes impeccable manners can get anyone through a public occasion, even a reaping.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Cinna: Katniss's stylist speaks softly and understands exactly what a costume can say to a crowd before its wearer opens her mouth.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Cato: A District 2 Career tribute trained to win the Games. He is used to treating physical dominance as proof that things are going according to plan.
book-suzanne-collins-the-hunger-games.Primrose Everdeen: Katniss's little sister is gentle with frightened animals and unusually composed around illness. At home she has already begun learning their mother's healing work.

book-stephenie-meyer-twilight.Bella Swan: A teenager newly arrived in rainy Forks who has long been used to looking after a parent. Curiosity takes her closer to danger than caution would allow.
book-stephenie-meyer-twilight.Edward Cullen: A vampire who hears other people's thoughts. Bella's unreadable mind fascinates him almost as much as her blood, and his self-control is under real strain.
book-stephenie-meyer-twilight.Alice Cullen: A vampire who glimpses possible futures. She greets Bella with the easy affection of someone who feels their friendship has already happened.
book-stephenie-meyer-twilight.James: A tracker among vampires who enjoys the ingenuity of a difficult hunt. Trying to protect his intended quarry only makes the pursuit more interesting to him.
book-stephenie-meyer-twilight.Carlisle Cullen: A vampire physician whose decades of disciplined practice let him work around blood. His adopted family looks to him for both restraint and refuge.
book-stephenie-meyer-twilight.Charlie Swan: Forks's police chief and Bella's father. He expresses affection in practical gestures and is entirely comfortable sharing a room without making conversation.
book-stephenie-meyer-twilight.Jacob Black: A Quileute teenager who likes repairing engines and makes Bella laugh. His easy company offers her an entry into a community with its own history.

book-f-scott-fitzgerald-the-great-gatsby.Jay Gatsby: A self-invented millionaire throws lavish parties in the hope of attracting one particular guest. His practised formality slips when Daisy finally arrives.
book-f-scott-fitzgerald-the-great-gatsby.Nick Carraway: A Midwesterner renting a little house on Long Island narrates his wealthy neighbours' affairs. His reluctance to judge sits uneasily with the precision of his judgments.
book-f-scott-fitzgerald-the-great-gatsby.Daisy Buchanan: A young woman whose light, carrying voice makes conversation feel intimate. Her affection for Gatsby competes with the extraordinary protection of inherited wealth.
book-f-scott-fitzgerald-the-great-gatsby.Tom Buchanan: A wealthy former athlete regards houses, women and points of view as things he has a right to possess. He reacts quickly to a challenge to that right.
book-f-scott-fitzgerald-the-great-gatsby.Jordan Baker: A professional golfer with an amused, detached manner. She moves between Daisy's and Nick's worlds with a competitive eye for other people's weaknesses.
book-f-scott-fitzgerald-the-great-gatsby.Myrtle Wilson: A garage owner's wife imagines a different self in the Manhattan apartment she shares with Tom. Clothes and company visibly alter her bearing.
book-f-scott-fitzgerald-the-great-gatsby.George Wilson: A mechanic in the valley of ashes depends on wealthier customers and loves his wife. He understands far less of her second life than the reader does.

book-george-orwell-nineteen-eighty-four.Winston Smith: A records clerk rewrites old news for the Party and privately tries to remember what happened. Starting a diary turns a vague doubt into a punishable act.
book-george-orwell-nineteen-eighty-four.Julia: A young woman performs public orthodoxy convincingly while carving out private pleasures. She is better than Winston at finding somewhere to meet unseen.
book-george-orwell-nineteen-eighty-four.O’Brien: An Inner Party member whose manner invites Winston to imagine a shared understanding. One ambiguous glance can sustain an extraordinary amount of hope.
book-george-orwell-nineteen-eighty-four.Mr. Charrington: An antiques dealer offers objects that seem to have survived official memory. His shop lets Winston imagine an ordinary private life almost lost to history.
book-george-orwell-nineteen-eighty-four.Tom Parsons: Winston's enthusiastic neighbour throws himself into community events and Party duties. His pride in his children's zeal is particularly unsettling.
book-george-orwell-nineteen-eighty-four.Syme: A lexicographer helping produce the new Newspeak dictionary takes open delight in eliminating words. He understands the political purpose of his work with dangerous clarity.

book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Harry Potter: Harry comes back to school under guard and wanting answers about his parents. Learning to face a Dementor means finding a memory powerful enough to hold on to.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Hermione Granger: A Muggle-born student arriving at Hogwarts exceptionally well prepared. Her determination to get the answer right masks a newcomer's anxiety about belonging.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Ron Weasley: The youngest Weasley son at Hogwarts has inherited robes, family stories and several reputations to live up to. At chess he gets to make the decisions.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Sirius Black: An escaped prisoner whose name sends the wizarding world into panic. Conflicting memories of his youth complicate the story Harry has been told.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Remus Lupin: A shabby, soft-spoken teacher who builds practical lessons around his pupils' fears. His kindness toward Harry carries memories of an earlier generation at school.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Peter Pettigrew: A schoolfriend of Harry's father remembered as the least imposing member of their group. Much about that friendship comes to Harry through other people's testimony.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Severus Snape: The Potions master speaks softly enough to make a classroom lean forward. Harry finds that the man already has strong feelings about a boy he barely knows.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Rubeus Hagrid: Hogwarts's enormous gamekeeper welcomes creatures that other people prudently avoid. Tenderness and an unfortunate inability to keep a secret make him Harry's first real friend.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Buckbeak: A hippogriff whose fierce response to disrespect makes introductions a matter of precise etiquette. Hagrid sees a magnificent creature where others see a liability.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Albus Dumbledore: The headmaster can put a nervous child at ease with an absurd remark. His apparent distraction rarely prevents him from noticing what matters.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Sybill Trelawney: The Divination teacher cultivates a mist of incense, veils and ominous suggestions. Even sceptical pupils have trouble forgetting a prediction made about them.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Cornelius Fudge: The Minister for Magic likes to project cheerful reassurance. When public confidence is at stake his concern for procedure can become quite selective.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Draco Malfoy: A wealthy first-year boy who arrives certain he knows which wizarding families matter. He expects other children to organize themselves around the same hierarchy.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Minerva McGonagall: The Transfiguration professor demands precision and enforces school rules without fuss. Her fierce interest in Gryffindor Quidditch occasionally produces a surprising exception.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Crookshanks: Hermione's large, bandy-legged cat takes a persistent interest in Ron's rat. His behaviour fuels a quarrel before anyone thinks to ask what he recognizes.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Marge Dursley: Vernon's visiting sister breeds dogs and confidently applies her theories of breeding to Harry. Her delight in needling him has spectacular consequences.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.Oliver Wood: Gryffindor's Keeper and Quidditch captain explains tactics with evangelical urgency. Finding a gifted Seeker matters considerably more to him than the Seeker's age.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.James Potter: Harry's late father emerges through his schoolfriends' memories as a gifted, mischievous boy. The stories offer Harry a new way to know a stranger he loves.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-pr.The Fat Lady: The portrait guarding Gryffindor Tower takes passwords, interruptions and attacks on her canvas seriously. School security depends on her willingness to open a door.

book-jane-austen-pride-and-prejudice.Elizabeth Bennet: The second Bennet daughter delights in the ridiculous and usually trusts her reading of a room. Discovering an error in her judgment is thoroughly uncomfortable.
book-jane-austen-pride-and-prejudice.Fitzwilliam Darcy: A wealthy, reserved landowner whose awkwardness reads as disdain. He is accustomed to having his good intentions understood without doing the work of explaining them.
book-jane-austen-pride-and-prejudice.Jane Bennet: Elizabeth's eldest sister instinctively supplies a charitable explanation for other people's behaviour. Her composure makes the depth of her own feelings easy to miss.
book-jane-austen-pride-and-prejudice.Charles Bingley: An amiable new neighbour delighted with nearly everyone he meets. Trust in his better-informed friends can keep him from acting on his own good judgment.
book-jane-austen-pride-and-prejudice.George Wickham: A handsome militia officer with a persuasive account of past injustice. He judges the sympathies of a new listener with remarkable speed.
book-jane-austen-pride-and-prejudice.Lydia Bennet: The youngest Bennet sister loves dancing, officers and the distinction of being first at anything. She has little notion of who bears the cost of her adventures.
book-jane-austen-pride-and-prejudice.Mrs. Bennet: A mother whose nerves rise and fall with her daughters' marriage prospects. Her embarrassing manoeuvres spring from an entirely real fear about their home.

book-colleen-hoover-it-ends-with-us.Lily Bloom: An aspiring florist who grew up watching her mother live with an abusive husband. Her determination to build a different life gets tested in intimate, ordinary moments.
book-colleen-hoover-it-ends-with-us.Ryle Kincaid: An ambitious neurosurgeon whose attention can feel intoxicating. His tenderness and his capacity for violence leave Lily making decisions he cannot make for her.
book-colleen-hoover-it-ends-with-us.Atlas Corrigan: A boy Lily befriended when he was homeless, now a chef. His ability to recognize what somebody needs has outlasted their years apart.
book-colleen-hoover-it-ends-with-us.Allysa Kincaid: Ryle's outgoing sister befriends Lily and helps at the flower shop. Loyalty becomes complicated when her friend and her brother need very different things.
book-colleen-hoover-it-ends-with-us.Marshall: Allysa's wealthy, good-humoured husband makes Lily feel at home in an unfamiliar social circle. He knows Ryle as both friend and family.

book-george-orwell-animal-farm.Napoleon: A taciturn pig invests in organization, enforcement and the training of young dogs. He is willing to let a rival make the more memorable speech.
book-george-orwell-animal-farm.Snowball: An energetic pig draws plans, organizes committees and argues for a windmill. His confidence in an idea's merits leaves him vulnerable to a different kind of contest.
book-george-orwell-animal-farm.Boxer: A powerful workhorse meets every setback by promising greater effort. Everyone relies on his strength, especially those who decide how it will be spent.
book-george-orwell-animal-farm.Squealer: A persuasive pig turns shortages, reversals and special privileges into evidence that the leadership deserves still more trust.
book-george-orwell-animal-farm.Clover: A maternal mare notices discrepancies between the animals' original promises and their present conditions. Her uncertain reading leaves her dependent on others to confirm what has changed.
book-george-orwell-animal-farm.Benjamin: An elderly donkey can read perfectly well and has little faith that a change of rulers will improve a donkey's lot. Boxer nevertheless matters deeply to him.
book-george-orwell-animal-farm.Old Major: An aging prize boar gathers the animals to describe a dream of freedom. His listeners must decide what political form that vision should take.

book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Harry Potter: Returning to Hogwarts after a summer cut off from his friends, Harry hears a voice nobody else can. Suspicion about his connection to Slytherin follows him through the corridors.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Ron Weasley: The youngest Weasley son at Hogwarts has inherited robes, family stories and several reputations to live up to. At chess he gets to make the decisions.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Hermione Granger: A Muggle-born student arriving at Hogwarts exceptionally well prepared. Her determination to get the answer right masks a newcomer's anxiety about belonging.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Ginny Weasley: Ron's younger sister knows a great deal about Harry before she meets him. At Hogwarts, being the youngest Weasley can feel unexpectedly lonely.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Lord Voldemort (Tom Riddle): The dark wizard whose attack left Harry orphaned and scarred. Even his name can make an otherwise talkative room fall silent.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Gilderoy Lockhart: A celebrity author teaching Defence Against the Dark Arts treats a dangerous encounter as an opportunity for a photograph, autograph or anecdote about himself.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Dobby: A house-elf trying to warn Harry of danger while bound to obey another family. Even an honest warning requires astonishing verbal and physical contortions.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Rubeus Hagrid: Hogwarts's enormous gamekeeper welcomes creatures that other people prudently avoid. Tenderness and an unfortunate inability to keep a secret make him Harry's first real friend.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Lucius Malfoy: Draco's father exerts influence through money, family pedigree and connections to Hogwarts's governors. His courtesy always leaves room for an insult.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Draco Malfoy: A wealthy first-year boy who arrives certain he knows which wizarding families matter. He expects other children to organize themselves around the same hierarchy.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Moaning Myrtle: A teenage ghost who haunts a girls' bathroom and remembers school humiliations vividly. Asking a tactless question can set an entire cubicle wailing.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Albus Dumbledore: The headmaster can put a nervous child at ease with an absurd remark. His apparent distraction rarely prevents him from noticing what matters.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Arthur Weasley: Ron's father works for the Ministry and finds Muggle technology endlessly fascinating. His delight in plugs and cars sometimes outpaces his understanding of their purpose.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Molly Weasley: The Weasley matriarch can add a place at her crowded table and deliver a devastating reprimand with equal conviction.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Fawkes: Dumbledore's phoenix experiences death and renewal as part of its natural life. Its song, tears and loyalty have properties unfamiliar to most wizards.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Aragog: An enormous talking spider raised by Hagrid. His gratitude toward one particular human does not extend automatically to Hagrid's visiting friends.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Colin Creevey: A Muggle-born first-year carrying a camera everywhere. His enthusiasm for Harry makes plain how odd it is to be a celebrity at school.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Argus Filch: The school caretaker knows its forbidden corridors and students' excuses intimately. His resentment has a private dimension that makes ridicule especially painful.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Justin Finch-Fletchley: A well-spoken Muggle-born Hufflepuff whose trust in Harry wavers when fear spreads through the school.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ch.Nearly Headless Nick: Gryffindor's resident ghost has courtly manners and a lasting grievance about an execution that failed to make him eligible for the Headless Hunt.

book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-thorns-and-.Feyre Archeron: A human hunter who feeds her family with a bow. Even when she is sizing up a threat, she notices colour and light like a painter.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-thorns-and-.Tamlin: The High Lord of Spring would sooner fight than explain himself. He plays the fiddle, and goes remarkably quiet when someone asks about his court.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-thorns-and-.Lucien Vanserra: Tamlin's red-haired emissary knows exactly which remark will break the tension at dinner and which will turn the whole table against him.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-thorns-and-.Rhysand: The High Lord of Night makes menace sound like flirtation. He likes the person across from him to wonder how much he already knows.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-thorns-and-.Amarantha: A faerie ruler who stages cruelty as court entertainment. She enjoys giving her prisoners a choice when she thinks she controls every outcome.

book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Bilbo Baggins: A comfortably housed hobbit drawn onto the road as a burglar. His small voice, good manners and talent for riddles prove surprisingly portable assets.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Gandalf: A wandering wizard who engineers unlikely meetings and has great faith in a hobbit's usefulness. His advice often becomes clear only after he has left.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Thorin Oakenshield: An exiled dwarf king who carries his people's dispossession as a personal duty. Formal courtesy can turn swiftly to pride where his ancestral treasure is concerned.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Smaug: A dragon who knows his hoard down to the last cup. He enjoys conversation, particularly when he can get a frightened intruder to say too much.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Bard the Bowman: A Lake-town bowman descended from the lords of Dale. Long familiarity with warnings nobody wants to hear has given him a reputation for grimness.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Gollum: A solitary creature beneath the mountains who talks to himself and treasures a small ring. A game of riddles briefly gives him company as well as prey.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Beorn: A skin-changer who lives with animals and receives strangers cautiously. Winning his hospitality requires a story told at exactly the right pace.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Thranduil: The woodland Elvenking imprisons Thorin's party when its explanations prove unsatisfactory. He has his own people's safety and treasure to consider.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Balin: An older dwarf with exceptionally sharp eyes who becomes one of Bilbo's earliest friends in the company. Praise from him feels earned.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Dwalin: The first dwarf through Bilbo's door arrives with a blue beard and an appetite. His unembarrassed hospitality in reverse sets the tone of the evening.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Fíli: One of Thorin's young nephews, often sent ahead to scout with his brother. His place in the company is both adventurous and familial.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Kíli: Fíli's brother is among the youngest dwarves on the expedition. The pair volunteer for jobs requiring agility and a good pair of eyes.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Dori: A strong dwarf repeatedly called upon to carry or recover Bilbo. He has a thoroughly understandable interest in who is responsible for the burglar this time.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Nori: A member of Thorin's company who plays the flute with Dori and Ori at Bag End. Bilbo first knows him as one more extraordinary dinner guest.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Ori: The third flautist at Bilbo's unexpected party. His place in the group links the homely music of Bag End to the dwarves' longing for their lost home.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Óin: A dwarf with a particular skill for making fire. On a wet expedition that practical gift matters rather more than an impressive introduction.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Glóin: Óin's brother doubts Bilbo's qualifications at the outset. His scepticism gives the hobbit an early reason to insist that he can be useful.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Bifur: A clarinet-playing member of the expedition who joins the music at Bag End. Like his companions he carries a claim on a home he has lost.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Bofur: Bombur's brother plays clarinet at the gathering that unsettles Bilbo's household. He shares the company's long marches, scant meals and dreadful river crossing.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Bombur: The company's heaviest dwarf plays a drum at Bag End. An enchanted sleep makes his safety on the trail a collective responsibility.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Elrond: The lord of Rivendell reads the moon-letters on Thorin's map. Learning, hospitality and a long memory are his particular gifts to travellers.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Dáin Ironfoot: Thorin's kinsman leads the dwarves of the Iron Hills. His decision to march gives a family claim the force of an approaching army.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Master of Lake-town: Lake-town's elected leader thinks in terms of trade, public sentiment and staying in office. A returning king makes all three calculations more difficult.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Great Goblin: The ruler beneath the Misty Mountains conducts interrogations before a noisy court. The sight of an old Elvish sword can transform his curiosity into fury.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Roäc: An elderly raven who remembers friendship between birds and dwarves. He carries intelligence about the mountain that no earthbound scout could gather.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-hobbit.Bolg: The son of Azog leads a goblin army toward the Lonely Mountain. His arrival forces rival claimants to take stock of a common enemy.

book-taylor-jenkins-reid-the-seven-husba.Evelyn Hugo: An aging Hollywood star hires an unexpected interviewer to tell the story behind her seven marriages. She knows exactly when to let a silence work for her.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-the-seven-husba.Monique Grant: A young magazine writer handed a career-making assignment on peculiar terms. Her growing admiration for Evelyn competes with her obligation to ask hard questions.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-the-seven-husba.Celia St. James: A gifted red-haired actress whose early rivalry with Evelyn becomes a more intimate connection. Her professional confidence has limits where Evelyn is concerned.

book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Peeta Mellark: Separated from Katniss, Peeta appears in Capitol broadcasts. She and the rebels watch the same interviews and hear quite different things in his voice.
book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Gale Hawthorne: Katniss's hunting partner sets ingenious snares. He shares her duty to feed a family and has a much greater appetite for open rebellion.
book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Alma Coin: The president of District 13 runs a tightly rationed society. She wants the rebellion to have a symbol and expects that symbol to take instructions.
book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Finnick Odair: A District 4 victor who plays the handsome celebrity with practised ease. A trident in his hands or a threat to someone he loves reveals another register.
book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Primrose Everdeen: Katniss's little sister is gentle with frightened animals and unusually composed around illness. At home she has already begun learning their mother's healing work.
book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Coriolanus Snow: Panem's president speaks quietly, prizes order and takes a personal interest in anyone capable of moving a crowd. His visits are heralded by white roses.
book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Boggs: A District 13 officer assigned to protect Katniss. He follows orders with a soldier's precision and gives her room to exercise her own judgment.
book-suzanne-collins-mockingjay.Haymitch Abernathy: District 12's surviving victor drinks heavily and notices everything. His abrasive coaching makes more sense once you understand whom the Games are designed to please.

book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Harry Potter: Private lessons with Dumbledore turn Harry into a student of an enemy's past. Meanwhile he is quite sure a classmate's present behaviour deserves investigation.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Albus Dumbledore: The headmaster can put a nervous child at ease with an absurd remark. His apparent distraction rarely prevents him from noticing what matters.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Severus Snape: The Potions master speaks softly enough to make a classroom lean forward. Harry finds that the man already has strong feelings about a boy he barely knows.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Draco Malfoy: A wealthy first-year boy who arrives certain he knows which wizarding families matter. He expects other children to organize themselves around the same hierarchy.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Horace Slughorn: A returning Potions master who collects promising pupils and influential acquaintances. His genuine pleasure in talent coexists with a habit of measuring social connections.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Hermione Granger: A Muggle-born student arriving at Hogwarts exceptionally well prepared. Her determination to get the answer right masks a newcomer's anxiety about belonging.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Ron Weasley: The youngest Weasley son at Hogwarts has inherited robes, family stories and several reputations to live up to. At chess he gets to make the decisions.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Ginny Weasley: Ron's younger sister knows a great deal about Harry before she meets him. At Hogwarts, being the youngest Weasley can feel unexpectedly lonely.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Lord Voldemort (Tom Riddle): The dark wizard whose attack left Harry orphaned and scarred. Even his name can make an otherwise talkative room fall silent.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Narcissa Malfoy: Draco's mother moves through pure-blood society with cool assurance. Fear for her son can drive her to take risks quite unlike her sister's.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Bellatrix Lestrange: A fervent Death Eater who treats cruelty as an expression of loyalty. The pride she takes in serving Voldemort overrides almost every family obligation.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Fenrir Greyback: A werewolf who embraces the terror attached to his condition and deliberately cultivates it. Lupin knows exactly why that choice matters.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Rufus Scrimgeour: The new Minister for Magic brings an Auror's bearing and a politician's need for an endorsement. He badly wants Harry seen on his side.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Lavender Brown: A Gryffindor who throws herself into a romance with Ron. Her unabashed affection makes private tensions among his friends conspicuously public.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Cormac McLaggen: A well-connected Gryffindor trying out for Keeper. He has advice for nearly every player on the pitch and little interest in receiving any himself.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Merope Gaunt: A young witch raised under her father's contempt whose longing for a nearby Muggle draws Harry into the history of Voldemort's family.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Morfin Gaunt: Merope's brother speaks Parseltongue and jealously guards his family's claims to Slytherin ancestry. Memory makes his testimony more complicated than it first appears.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Marvolo Gaunt: The impoverished head of the Gaunt family treats bloodline and heirlooms as proof of greatness. His daughter bears the brunt of his humiliation.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Hepzibah Smith: A wealthy collector who enjoys showing prized magical objects to an admiring young visitor. Her memories connect social vanity with the trade in important relics.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Rubeus Hagrid: Hogwarts's enormous gamekeeper welcomes creatures that other people prudently avoid. Tenderness and an unfortunate inability to keep a secret make him Harry's first real friend.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Katie Bell: An experienced Gryffindor Chaser whose ordinary Hogsmeade outing becomes evidence of a danger reaching inside the school.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Bill Weasley: The eldest Weasley sibling is a curse-breaker with an earring and a relaxed manner that revise Harry's idea of what a responsible adult looks like.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Fleur Delacour: A Beauxbatons champion whose poise is mistaken for vanity. Concern for her little sister reveals how seriously she takes responsibility for someone else.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Nymphadora Tonks: A young Auror who can alter her appearance and still trips over things. Her informality offers Harry a different model of adulthood in wartime.
book-j-k-rowling-harry-potter-and-the-ha.Remus Lupin: A shabby, soft-spoken teacher who builds practical lessons around his pupils' fears. His kindness toward Harry carries memories of an earlier generation at school.

book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Amir: A Kabul boy who wants to be a writer and longs for his father's approval. He tells his story as a man still judging a childhood choice.
book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Hassan: The son of a Hazara servant is a gifted kite runner. He reads Amir's moods with a loyalty that Amir finds both comforting and difficult to deserve.
book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Baba: Amir's imposing father prizes courage and generosity. Migration tests which parts of his public confidence he can carry into a much smaller life.
book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Ali: Hassan's father has served Baba's household for years. His restrained dignity exposes the gulf between being treated affectionately and being treated as an equal.
book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Rahim Khan: Baba's friend is the first adult to take Amir's writing seriously. He offers a quieter kind of attention than the boy receives from his father.
book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Soraya: A young Afghan woman in California whose honesty about her past challenges Amir. Their shared exile gives them a language their parents also understand.
book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Assef: A neighbourhood bully who uses ethnic supremacy to justify cruelty. He enjoys making witnesses feel implicated in what they are frightened to stop.
book-khaled-hosseini-the-kite-runner.Sohrab: Hassan's young son has inherited his father's skill with a slingshot. Trust is a great deal harder for him to offer than adults expect.

book-gillian-flynn-gone-girl.Amy Dunne: The missing woman at the centre of a media frenzy grew up sharing her name with her parents' fictional heroine. She knows how stories shape expectations.
book-gillian-flynn-gone-girl.Nick Dunne: Amy's husband struggles to perform the role of distraught spouse convincingly. A badly timed smile can undo an entire interview.
book-gillian-flynn-gone-girl.Margo Dunne: Nick's twin sister and business partner knows the man behind his public expressions. Loyalty does not stop her questioning his account.
book-gillian-flynn-gone-girl.Desi Collings: A wealthy former boyfriend remembers Amy with unnerving precision. He can offer sanctuary on terms shaped by his own idea of her.
book-gillian-flynn-gone-girl.Rhonda Boney: The lead detective on Amy's disappearance listens patiently and keeps noticing where Nick's account leaves gaps.
book-gillian-flynn-gone-girl.Tanner Bolt: A defence lawyer famous for representing men accused of killing their wives. He understands a television audience almost as well as a jury.

book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Feyre Archeron: Feyre has come home with new strength and memories she cannot leave behind. Learning how to use that strength means deciding whom she trusts to teach her.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Rhysand: The High Lord of Night makes menace sound like flirtation. He likes the person across from him to wonder how much he already knows.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Morrigan: Mor is Rhysand's cousin and a practised court emissary. She can make a stranger feel welcome in a room full of people with secrets.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Cassian: An Illyrian general who grew up fighting for a place in the ranks. He teases his closest friends and takes a recruit's training seriously.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Azriel: The Night Court's spymaster lets other people fill a silence. Shadows gather around him, and his quiet attention can feel tender or unnerving.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Amren: An ancient being in a small faerie body, Amren studies dead languages, hoards jewels and has little patience for anyone wasting her time.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Tamlin: The High Lord of Spring would sooner fight than explain himself. He plays the fiddle, and goes remarkably quiet when someone asks about his court.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-mist-and-fu.Nesta Archeron: Feyre's eldest sister can find the one sentence that will wound somebody. Asking that same person for help costs her almost more than she can bear.

book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-with-the-dra.Lisbeth Salander: A freelance investigator and gifted hacker who remembers insults and details with equal precision. She guards her autonomy fiercely after years of official interference.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-with-the-dra.Mikael Blomkvist: A journalist facing a professional disgrace accepts a wealthy industrialist's old family mystery. He gets people talking by actually listening to them.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-with-the-dra.Henrik Vanger: The elderly patriarch of an industrial family remains haunted by his niece's disappearance. He has had decades to organize the evidence and cultivate his suspicions.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-with-the-dra.Harriet Vanger: The teenager who disappeared from the Vanger family's island gathering. Photographs and other people's memories offer a partial, sometimes misleading portrait of her.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-with-the-dra.Martin Vanger: Harriet's brother now runs the family company. He receives visitors with the polished assurance of a man accustomed to speaking for an institution.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-with-the-dra.Erika Berger: Mikael's editor, business partner and longtime lover. She has to weigh his investigative instincts against the survival of the magazine they built.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-with-the-dra.Nils Bjurman: Lisbeth's court-appointed guardian controls access to her money. He exploits the immense difference between how officials see him and how she experiences his power.

book-dan-brown-angels-demons.Robert Langdon: A Harvard symbologist who reads paintings, architecture and ritual objects as puzzles. His scholarly delight survives in remarkably inconvenient circumstances.
book-dan-brown-angels-demons.Vittoria Vetra: An Italian scientist racing to recover antimatter stolen after her father's murder. She is as comfortable explaining the experiment as Langdon is deciphering its symbols.
book-dan-brown-angels-demons.Carlo Ventresca: The late pope's camerlengo suddenly speaks for the Vatican during a crisis. His personal conviction has enormous appeal in a frightened room.
book-dan-brown-angels-demons.Maximilian Kohler: CERN's director is impatient with superstition and unwilling to let a threat to his institution go unanswered. He summons Langdon on the strength of a symbol.
book-dan-brown-angels-demons.Commander Olivetti: The Swiss Guard commander charged with keeping a conclave safe. He needs actionable intelligence and has little patience for a visiting scholar's speculations.
book-dan-brown-angels-demons.Hassassin: An assassin commissioned to turn a series of killings into a public spectacle. His sense of historical grievance gives the work a private meaning.

book-paula-hawkins-the-girl-on-the-train.Rachel Watson: An unemployed commuter watches a couple from a train and imagines their life. When a woman disappears, Rachel must separate observation from fantasy and missing memory.
book-paula-hawkins-the-girl-on-the-train.Megan Hipwell: The woman in the house beside the tracks feels trapped by the domestic life Rachel envies. She shares her least comfortable memories with very few people.
book-paula-hawkins-the-girl-on-the-train.Anna Watson: Tom's new wife wants safety for her baby and an end to Rachel's intrusions. The same neighbourhood looks quite different from inside her house.
book-paula-hawkins-the-girl-on-the-train.Tom Watson: Rachel's former husband has built a new family in their old home. He often serves as the authority on events Rachel cannot remember.
book-paula-hawkins-the-girl-on-the-train.Scott Hipwell: Megan's husband responds to her disappearance with grief that can turn possessive. Rachel's offer of information makes their dependence on each other precarious.
book-paula-hawkins-the-girl-on-the-train.Kamal Abdic: Megan's therapist listens to a version of her history unavailable to her neighbours. Professional confidentiality puts him in a difficult position when she vanishes.

book-william-golding-lord-of-the-flies.Ralph: The island's elected leader tries to keep shelters and the rescue fire in everyone's mind. Authority proves much harder than holding the conch.
book-william-golding-lord-of-the-flies.Jack Merridew: A choir leader accustomed to instant obedience discovers the exhilaration of hunting. The promise of meat gives the boys another reason to follow him.
book-william-golding-lord-of-the-flies.Piggy: A practical, articulate boy whose glasses can start a fire. The others depend on his insight while treating his need for acceptance as a weakness.
book-william-golding-lord-of-the-flies.Simon: A quiet boy drawn to solitude and to helping younger children. He is unusually willing to look directly at what the group has decided to fear.
book-william-golding-lord-of-the-flies.Roger: A withdrawn older boy tests what happens when he throws stones near someone. The gradual disappearance of consequences changes how close he aims.
book-william-golding-lord-of-the-flies.Sam: One of the twins assigned to keep watch. He borrows confidence from his brother, but shared fear makes their testimony easy for stronger boys to shape.
book-william-golding-lord-of-the-flies.Eric: Sam's twin tends the fire and speaks in tandem with him. As loyalties harden, staying beside his brother becomes a survival decision of its own.

book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Frodo Baggins: Bilbo's heir is a hobbit with a taste for Elvish stories and an unusually strong sense of responsibility. Inheriting a ring gives that quality a terrible test.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Samwise Gamgee: Frodo's gardener loves growing things, listening to tales and making sure his master eats. His plain speech is capable of startling poetic feeling.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Gandalf: A wandering wizard who engineers unlikely meetings and has great faith in a hobbit's usefulness. His advice often becomes clear only after he has left.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Aragorn: A weatherbeaten Ranger called Strider keeps watch over people who scarcely know he protects them. He must earn the hobbits' trust without the privileges of rank.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Meriadoc Brandybuck: Frodo's practical cousin has thought ahead about the journey, the cover story and the baggage. His cheerfulness is backed by real preparations.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Peregrin Took: The youngest of the four hobbits brings curiosity, appetite and an imperfect sense of when to keep quiet. Courage is rarely his first impulse but often his second.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Boromir: Gondor's proud captain has seen what war costs his people. He considers every discovery in terms of whether it might help defend his city.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Legolas: An elven archer from the Woodland Realm hears and sees what his companions miss. Friendship on the road challenges an inherited suspicion of dwarves.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Gimli: Glóin's son represents his people with a warrior's pride and a craftsman's feeling for beautiful stone. Moria is family history for him.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Bilbo Baggins: The burglar has become an elderly storyteller with a well-stocked pantry. Leaving home again means parting with a possession he finds very hard to surrender.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Elrond: The lord of Rivendell reads the moon-letters on Thorin's map. Learning, hospitality and a long memory are his particular gifts to travellers.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Galadriel: The Lady of Lórien offers shelter and a disconcertingly searching welcome. Her understanding of desire makes her refusal or acceptance of a gift intensely consequential.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Tom Bombadil: An ancient, singing inhabitant of the Old Forest who helps the hobbits without sharing their fear of the Ring or their sense of a deadline.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Goldberry: The River-woman's daughter welcomes the hobbits to a table where weather and song seem intimately connected. Her composure lends the house its distinctive peace.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Glorfindel: An Elf-lord rides out from Rivendell to help the hunted Ring-bearer reach safety. The book gives him a crucial encounter on the road to the Ford.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Barliman Butterbur: The forgetful but good-hearted landlord of the Prancing Pony knows the business of Bree exceptionally well. Delivering a particular message proves another matter.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.The Witch-king of Angmar: The chief of the Ringwraiths pursues the Ring-bearer with terrifying persistence. Riders, weather and the courage of his opponents change in his presence.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Saruman: The head of the order of wizards has studied the Enemy closely. His persuasive voice can make accommodation with power sound like clear-sighted prudence.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Haldir: An elven guard at the edge of Lórien must reconcile the rules of a guarded realm with the needs of a deeply unusual group of travellers.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Celeborn: Galadriel's husband and co-ruler receives the Fellowship in Lórien. Grief over events in Moria initially colours his judgment of its dwarven survivor.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Arwen: Elrond's daughter is glimpsed at Rivendell through a hobbit's eyes. Her quiet connection to Aragorn hints at the private stakes of his long service.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Durin's Bane: The ancient terror awakened beneath Moria. Its arrival changes an orderly retreat into a confrontation beyond the power of almost everyone present.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Fredegar Bolger: A hobbit who helps Frodo's friends arrange the departure and stays behind at Crickhollow. Covering someone else's tracks proves a dangerous assignment.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-fellowship-of-the.Gildor Inglorion: An Elf travelling west who shelters the hobbits early in their journey. His reluctance to give direct counsel comes with a clear-eyed assessment of their danger.

book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Lucy Pevensie: The youngest Pevensie is the first to enter the wardrobe. She treats a faun's invitation to tea with the same seriousness she hopes her siblings will grant her.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Edmund Pevensie: A younger brother who resents being laughed at. The promise of sweets, importance and an audience willing to hear his grievances proves dangerously attractive.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Peter Pevensie: The eldest Pevensie feels responsible for the others' safety. He must learn when leadership means accepting that his youngest sister saw something he did not.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Susan Pevensie: A practical older sister inclined to weigh an alarming story before acting on it. In Narnia she discovers she has a particular gift for archery.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Aslan: A great lion whose name arouses a different feeling in each child. His authority leaves room for tenderness, play and acts nobody else understands in advance.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Jadis (the White Witch): Narnia's ruler holds the country in perpetual winter. She can sound remarkably solicitous when a lonely child has something she wants.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Mr. Tumnus: A faun with parcels and an umbrella invites Lucy home. The obligations of hospitality bring him face to face with orders he is ashamed to obey.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Mr. Beaver: A cautious talking beaver recognizes the children and guides them to shelter. He explains Narnian politics by the fire after supper.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Mrs. Beaver: A hospitable beaver with an eye for what a travelling party will actually need. Even flight from the Witch calls for sensible provisions.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Digory Kirke: The elderly professor sheltering the evacuees listens to their dispute about Lucy. His habit of taking a child's logic seriously surprises the older children.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Maugrim: The wolf who commands the Witch's secret police turns pursuit into an official duty. His arrival makes a warm household immediately dangerous.
book-c-s-lewis-the-lion-the-witch-and-th.Father Christmas: His arrival with a sledge and carefully chosen gifts gives the children tangible evidence that the Witch's winter is weakening.

book-kathryn-stockett-the-help.Aibileen Clark: A Black domestic worker in Jackson has raised generations of white children. Her measured voice carries a grief and judgment her employers seldom hear.
book-kathryn-stockett-the-help.Minny Jackson: A talented cook whose sharp replies have cost her jobs. Behind the comic timing is an acute understanding of the price of speaking freely.
book-kathryn-stockett-the-help.Eugenia Phelan: An aspiring white writer, nicknamed Skeeter, asks domestic workers to tell their stories. Her freedom to ask does not protect the women who answer.
book-kathryn-stockett-the-help.Hilly Holbrook: A socially powerful organizer who makes racist domestic rules into tests of friendship. She can threaten a livelihood while arranging a charity event.
book-kathryn-stockett-the-help.Celia Foote: A newcomer shunned by Jackson society hires Minny in secret. Glamour and apparent ineptitude conceal a woman trying hard to build a family.
book-kathryn-stockett-the-help.Elizabeth Leefolt: Aibileen's employer wants the right friends and a respectable home. Her anxiety about approval affects both her little daughter and the woman raising her.

book-ray-bradbury-fahrenheit-451.Guy Montag: A fireman paid to burn books starts noticing the questions his daily work suppresses. At home he has little language for the dissatisfaction those questions expose.
book-ray-bradbury-fahrenheit-451.Captain Beatty: Montag's captain is widely read enough to quote the literature he destroys. He uses that knowledge to make doubt look both predictable and pointless.
book-ray-bradbury-fahrenheit-451.Clarisse McClellan: A teenage neighbour takes walks, watches people and asks Montag whether he is happy. Her attention to small things makes the question difficult to dismiss.
book-ray-bradbury-fahrenheit-451.Mildred Montag: Montag's wife calls the figures on her wall screens family. She has learned to keep distress out of conversation, even when her own life is at risk.
book-ray-bradbury-fahrenheit-451.Faber: A retired English professor knows what has been lost with the books. Helping Montag forces him to reckon with earlier decisions to stay quiet.
book-ray-bradbury-fahrenheit-451.Granger: The leader of a wandering group preserving books through memory. His patient sense of historical time offers Montag an alternative to the city's frantic present.

book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.Feyre Archeron: Back at the Spring Court, Feyre must let old friends see the version of her they expect while listening for information that could save her other home.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.Rhysand: The High Lord of Night makes menace sound like flirtation. He likes the person across from him to wonder how much he already knows.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.Nesta Archeron: Feyre's eldest sister can find the one sentence that will wound somebody. Asking that same person for help costs her almost more than she can bear.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.Elain Archeron: Feyre's sister tends gardens and remembers small kindnesses. Her family often makes decisions for her before anyone thinks to ask what she wants.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.Lucien Vanserra: Tamlin's red-haired emissary knows exactly which remark will break the tension at dinner and which will turn the whole table against him.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.King of Hybern: An ancient faerie monarch bent on restoring dominion over humans. He discusses enslavement with the composure of a ruler settling a boundary dispute.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.Cassian: An Illyrian general who grew up fighting for a place in the ranks. He teases his closest friends and takes a recruit's training seriously.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-wings-and-r.Amren: An ancient being in a small faerie body, Amren studies dead languages, hoards jewels and has little patience for anyone wasting her time.

book-markus-zusak-the-book-thief.Liesel Meminger: A girl fostered in Nazi Germany learns to read with her new father. Stealing a book becomes inseparable from keeping someone she loves close.
book-markus-zusak-the-book-thief.Death: The narrator collects the dead and notices the colours of the sky. Weariness with the scale of the work gives way to curiosity about one girl.
book-markus-zusak-the-book-thief.Hans Hubermann: A house painter and accordion player whose patience makes reading lessons possible. He understands the danger of kindness and extends it anyway.
book-markus-zusak-the-book-thief.Rosa Hubermann: Liesel's foster mother does laundry, swears magnificently and keeps a frightened household functioning. Affection seldom arrives in the form of a compliment.
book-markus-zusak-the-book-thief.Rudy Steiner: Liesel's neighbour is a fast runner, an admirer of Jesse Owens and a determined collector of opportunities to ask for a kiss.
book-markus-zusak-the-book-thief.Max Vandenburg: A young Jewish man in hiding finds common ground with Liesel through drawings and stories. An imagined boxing ring gives his anger somewhere to go.
book-markus-zusak-the-book-thief.Ilsa Hermann: The mayor's grieving wife opens her library to Liesel. Books permit a kind of contact that ordinary conversation often cannot.

book-john-steinbeck-of-mice-and-men.George Milton: A migrant ranch hand travels with Lennie and supplies the quick explanations that keep them employed. A shared dream of land helps him carry the responsibility.
book-john-steinbeck-of-mice-and-men.Lennie Small: A powerful worker with an intellectual disability finds comfort in soft textures and familiar stories. He wants badly to remember the rules George gives him.
book-john-steinbeck-of-mice-and-men.Candy: An aging ranch worker has lost a hand and fears outliving his usefulness. The men's plan offers a place where his savings could buy belonging.
book-john-steinbeck-of-mice-and-men.Curley: The boss's son is an amateur boxer who reads a bigger man's silence as a challenge. His position lets him pick fights others cannot refuse.
book-john-steinbeck-of-mice-and-men.Curley’s wife: A young woman known on the ranch only through her marriage looks for someone who will listen. She remembers a version of her future that included acting.
book-john-steinbeck-of-mice-and-men.Crooks: The Black stable hand lives separately from the other workers. Isolation has made him protective of his room and painfully susceptible to a promise of company.
book-john-steinbeck-of-mice-and-men.Slim: A mule driver whose skill gives him authority that requires no title. George trusts him with a confidence he has shared with almost nobody else.

book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Violet Sorrengail: Returning to Basgiath with information she cannot safely share, Violet has to survive interrogation as well as training. Keeping secrets from friends costs her most.
book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Xaden Riorson: A dragon rider and the son of an executed rebel. As wingleader, he bears responsibility for cadets who share the mark of their parents' rebellion.
book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Brennan Sorrengail: Violet's older brother is a gifted mender. He has to find a way to speak to her as both family and a military officer.
book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Burton Varrish: Basgiath's vice commandant brings an interrogator's patience to school discipline. His politeness makes it difficult for cadets to know when a test has begun.
book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Catriona Cordella: A gryphon flier with royal ties and history with Xaden. She knows how to turn somebody else's insecurity into an opening.
book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Tairn: An enormous black dragon with a short temper and a veteran's expectations. His blunt exchanges with Violet have the familiarity of an old argument.
book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Andarna: A young dragon drawn to Violet. Curiosity gives her questions a directness that can cut straight through the older dragons' solemnity.
book-rebecca-yarros-iron-flame.Lilith Sorrengail: Violet's mother is a general first in almost every room she enters. Even her attempts to keep her children safe sound like orders.

book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Eddard Stark: The lord of Winterfell takes an executioner's duty personally. A summons from an old friend brings his northern sense of obligation into a court that trades in secrets.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Catelyn Stark: Lady of Winterfell, born a Tully, she reads politics through kinship, promises and danger to her children. Urgency can make her act before her allies are ready.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Jon Snow: Raised as Ned Stark's bastard, Jon knows the household intimately while remaining conscious of his place at its edge. The Night's Watch offers a different brotherhood.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Daenerys Targaryen: An exiled Targaryen girl traded into marriage by her brother. Learning another language and another people's customs gives her room to discover authority of her own.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Tyrion Lannister: A wealthy lord's son with dwarfism has learned to enter a room anticipating the joke. Books, money and a precise insult are among his defences.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Arya Stark: A lord's daughter who would rather learn swordplay than needlework. She pays more attention to servants, animals and escapes than her elders realize.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Sansa Stark: Arya's older sister loves songs of gallant knights and knows how a lady should behave. At court, courtesy acquires uses her songs never taught her.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Bran Stark: A boy who loves climbing the walls of Winterfell and imagining himself a knight. His connection to his direwolf grows harder to explain.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Robb Stark: The eldest Stark son has learned to command beside his father. When adults look to him for decisions, the distance between boy and lord shrinks abruptly.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Robert Baratheon: A former rebel and formidable warrior who dislikes the daily business of kingship. He remembers his youth with Ned more fondly than he inhabits his marriage.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Cersei Lannister: The queen guards her children and her position with equal ferocity. A lifetime of watching her twin receive freedoms denied to her feeds her political ambition.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Jaime Lannister: A gifted knight known chiefly for killing the king he swore to guard. His insolence makes an effective shield against other people's certainty about his motives.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Joffrey Baratheon: The crown prince has been told all his life that deference is his due. He is especially dangerous when an audience witnesses an embarrassment.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Petyr Baelish: The master of coin has risen much further than his birth promised. He speaks of old affections as easily as he moves money and information.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Khal Drogo: A Dothraki warlord whose power rests on horsemanship and the allegiance of his riders. His new wife must learn to address him across language and custom.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Viserys Targaryen: Daenerys's older brother regards a lost throne as his property. Dependence on other people's hospitality gives his grand pronouncements a desperate edge.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Sandor Clegane: A scarred fighter in royal service who despises the pretty language of knighthood. His bitter candour unsettles children taught to admire men with swords.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Jorah Mormont: An exiled Westerosi knight familiar with Dothraki custom. Serving the young Targaryens offers him purpose, though his attachments and interests do not always align.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-game-of-thrones.Varys: The court's master of whispers collects the news everybody else overlooks. He can change his voice and social manner as readily as he changes a disguise.

book-sarah-j-maas-throne-of-glass.Celaena Sardothien (Aelin Galathynius): An assassin pulled from a labour camp to compete at court. She loves books, fine clothes and the look on someone's face when they underestimate her.
book-sarah-j-maas-throne-of-glass.Dorian Havilliard: Adarlan's crown prince reads voraciously and flirts easily. Behind the good manners is a young man beginning to question the father he will succeed.
book-sarah-j-maas-throne-of-glass.Chaol Westfall: The captain of the royal guard trusts training, order and his oldest friend Dorian. A divided loyalty can unsettle him more than an armed opponent.
book-sarah-j-maas-throne-of-glass.Nehemia Ytger: A princess of Eyllwe visiting the conquering court. Her apparent ease with ceremony leaves courtiers guessing how much of their conversation she understands.
book-sarah-j-maas-throne-of-glass.Kaltain Rompier: An ambitious young noblewoman who knows that the right marriage could secure her future. She studies royal favour as carefully as a general studies terrain.
book-sarah-j-maas-throne-of-glass.Cain: A brutal competitor sponsored by the Duke of Perrington. He expects size, intimidation and his patron's influence to carry him through the king's contest.

book-matt-haig-the-midnight-library.Nora Seed: A disheartened former musician finds shelves full of lives she might have led. Trying them requires discovering whose ambitions each imagined future actually fulfilled.
book-matt-haig-the-midnight-library.Mrs. Elm: The school librarian Nora trusted as a child appears as her guide among possible lives. She knows when a question is more helpful than an answer.
book-matt-haig-the-midnight-library.Joe Seed: Nora's older brother once shared a band with her. Their estrangement makes it hard to distinguish her regret about music from her regret about him.
book-matt-haig-the-midnight-library.Dan Lord: Nora's former fiancé dreamed of running a country pub. One possible life lets her discover how the reality compares with his account of the dream.
book-matt-haig-the-midnight-library.Izzy Hirsh: Nora's friend moved to Australia, where the two had imagined a life together. Distance has given Nora plenty of time to idealize the missed turn.
book-matt-haig-the-midnight-library.Ash: A surgeon whose small act of kindness stands out on Nora's worst evening. His significance differs strikingly across the lives available to her.

book-dan-brown-the-da-vinci-code.Robert Langdon: A Harvard symbologist who reads paintings, architecture and ritual objects as puzzles. His scholarly delight survives in remarkably inconvenient circumstances.
book-dan-brown-the-da-vinci-code.Sophie Neveu: A French police cryptologist with a personal link to the Louvre victim. Family memories supply meanings no expert could extract from the symbols alone.
book-dan-brown-the-da-vinci-code.Leigh Teabing: A wealthy Grail scholar with a theatrical manner and a long-nursed theory. He enjoys being the person who knows what the others have missed.
book-dan-brown-the-da-vinci-code.Silas: A religious zealot who believes violence can be an act of obedience. His fierce gratitude to the man who rescued him makes him vulnerable to direction.
book-dan-brown-the-da-vinci-code.Bézu Fache: A French police captain convinced the evidence points to Langdon. He commands a room through stillness and expects suspects to contradict themselves.
book-dan-brown-the-da-vinci-code.Jacques Saunière: The Louvre curator leaves an elaborate final message. His intricate games with his granddaughter provide a private language hidden inside familiar works of art.
book-dan-brown-the-da-vinci-code.Bishop Aringarosa: An Opus Dei bishop anxious about his organization's future. His sense of responsibility for Silas makes promises of powerful help especially persuasive.

book-margaret-atwood-the-handmaids-tale.Offred: A woman forced to bear children in Gilead preserves her earlier life through memories, secret jokes and an acute ear for forbidden words.
book-margaret-atwood-the-handmaids-tale.Serena Joy: The Commander's wife once addressed public audiences. Now confined to domestic authority, she exercises it over a woman whose presence she resents and requires.
book-margaret-atwood-the-handmaids-tale.The Commander: A senior official invites his Handmaid into private diversions. His loneliness is real, as is his ability to punish her for refusing.
book-margaret-atwood-the-handmaids-tale.Moira: Offred's friend from the time before Gilead meets coercion with irreverence and open rebellion. Memories of her nerve become a private resource.
book-margaret-atwood-the-handmaids-tale.Nick: The household's driver moves easily through spaces where Offred must ask permission. A small gesture from him can mean attraction, warning or surveillance.
book-margaret-atwood-the-handmaids-tale.Ofglen: Offred's assigned shopping partner trades prescribed greetings on the pavement. Whether a second meaning lies beneath them is a potentially lethal question.
book-margaret-atwood-the-handmaids-tale.Aunt Lydia: An instructor at the Red Centre who packages coercion as concern for women's safety. Her sayings persist in Offred's mind long after lessons end.

book-louisa-may-alcott-little-women.Jo March: The second March sister writes plays, hurries into arguments and wants to earn money with her pen. Love of home contends with impatience to see the world.
book-louisa-may-alcott-little-women.Meg March: The eldest March sister works as a governess and feels the pull of fashionable company. She has to decide what the domestic happiness she wants will cost.
book-louisa-may-alcott-little-women.Beth March: A shy pianist devoted to family, dolls and small acts of service. People discover how much she does most clearly when she is absent.
book-louisa-may-alcott-little-women.Amy March: The youngest sister wants to make art and move gracefully in society. Ambition, aesthetic sensitivity and a sharp sense of injury all begin early.
book-louisa-may-alcott-little-women.Theodore “Laurie” Laurence: The lonely boy next door finds a place in the March household. His money opens doors that affection and musical talent cannot always carry him through.
book-louisa-may-alcott-little-women.Marmee March: Mrs. March guides her daughters through financial and wartime strain. She can counsel Jo about anger because she knows the feeling intimately.
book-louisa-may-alcott-little-women.Friedrich Bhaer: A German professor Jo meets in New York takes her writing seriously enough to tell her when a story troubles him. His warmth is conspicuously unshowy.

book-charlotte-bronte-jane-eyre.Jane Eyre: A governess with little money and a rigorous sense of her own worth. The calm voice in which she answers an insult can carry years of anger.
book-charlotte-bronte-jane-eyre.Edward Rochester: Thornfield's master tests Jane with abrupt questions, invented scenarios and flashes of startling candour. He wants to be known while still keeping control of his secrets.
book-charlotte-bronte-jane-eyre.St. John Rivers: An austere clergyman drawn to missionary work. His admiration for Jane's abilities leaves little room for her to decline the life he has designed.
book-charlotte-bronte-jane-eyre.Bertha Mason: A Jamaican-born woman confined at Thornfield and described largely by people with an interest in her confinement. Her presence unsettles the house's respectable order.
book-charlotte-bronte-jane-eyre.Helen Burns: Jane's schoolfriend at Lowood meets cruelty with a patience that both inspires and infuriates her. Their conversations give Jane an intimate encounter with a different faith.
book-charlotte-bronte-jane-eyre.Adèle Varens: Jane's young French-speaking pupil enjoys songs, presents and an audience. Looking after her brings a daily domestic rhythm to Thornfield's mysteries.

book-colleen-hoover-ugly-love.Tate Collins: A nurse moving in with her brother agrees to a strictly limited relationship with his neighbour. She finds the rule against asking questions particularly hard.
book-colleen-hoover-ugly-love.Miles Archer: An airline pilot who manages risk professionally and tries to do the same with intimacy. He will discuss almost anything except his past.
book-colleen-hoover-ugly-love.Corbin Collins: Tate's older brother is a pilot who offers her a home. His protective streak makes the attraction between her and his friend an awkward secret.
book-colleen-hoover-ugly-love.Rachel: The girl Miles loved as a teenager. Their early scenes need the unguarded excitement of two people making plans before they understand the stakes.
book-colleen-hoover-ugly-love.Cap: An older elevator attendant who sees the building's residents come and go. His easy conversation gives Tate a place to think out loud.

book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-frost-and-s.Feyre Archeron: A painter helping rebuild Velaris after war, Feyre wants her family together for the Solstice. Neither wounds nor family estrangements obey the holiday calendar.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-frost-and-s.Rhysand: The High Lord of Night makes menace sound like flirtation. He likes the person across from him to wonder how much he already knows.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-frost-and-s.Cassian: An Illyrian general who grew up fighting for a place in the ranks. He teases his closest friends and takes a recruit's training seriously.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-frost-and-s.Nesta Archeron: Feyre's eldest sister can find the one sentence that will wound somebody. Asking that same person for help costs her almost more than she can bear.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-frost-and-s.Morrigan: Mor is Rhysand's cousin and a practised court emissary. She can make a stranger feel welcome in a room full of people with secrets.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-frost-and-s.Elain Archeron: Feyre's sister tends gardens and remembers small kindnesses. Her family often makes decisions for her before anyone thinks to ask what she wants.

book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-silver-flam.Nesta Archeron: Nesta would rather clear an impossible staircase than admit how much she is hurting. In the training ring she finds women willing to meet her on those terms.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-silver-flam.Cassian: An Illyrian general who grew up fighting for a place in the ranks. He teases his closest friends and takes a recruit's training seriously.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-silver-flam.Gwyneth Berdara: A priestess with a ringing singing voice, Gwyn brings curiosity and a fierce competitive streak to the training ring.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-silver-flam.Emerie: An Illyrian shopkeeper who knows what her village expects of women. She earns trust through practical generosity and turns up to train despite the gossip.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-silver-flam.Eris Vanserra: The Autumn Court's heir negotiates under his father's eye. Even a generous offer from him leaves its recipient looking for the price.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-silver-flam.Briallyn: A former human queen desperate to reverse the toll the Cauldron took on her body. She has considerable patience for a well-laid revenge.
book-sarah-j-maas-a-court-of-silver-flam.Feyre Archeron: A human hunter who feeds her family with a bow. Even when she is sizing up a threat, she notices colour and light like a painter.

book-emily-bronte-wuthering-heights.Heathcliff: A foundling raised at Wuthering Heights comes to know both intimacy and deliberate humiliation there. His long memory turns an old injury into a household inheritance.
book-emily-bronte-wuthering-heights.Catherine Earnshaw: Heathcliff's childhood companion feels most herself with him on the moors. Her sense of their inseparability coexists with a clear understanding of what marriage can buy.
book-emily-bronte-wuthering-heights.Edgar Linton: A cultivated neighbour whose gentleness offers Catherine a different kind of home. His capacity for endurance can be mistaken for mere softness.
book-emily-bronte-wuthering-heights.Cathy Linton: Catherine's daughter grows up sheltered at the Grange with a strong curiosity about the world outside it. She has both her mother's spirit and a capacity for repair.
book-emily-bronte-wuthering-heights.Hareton Earnshaw: Hindley's son has been denied the education and status of his birth. Shame makes him bristle at precisely the company from which he hopes to learn.
book-emily-bronte-wuthering-heights.Nelly Dean: A servant in both households narrates much of their history. Her interventions matter nearly as much as the events she tells her listener she merely witnessed.
book-emily-bronte-wuthering-heights.Isabella Linton: Edgar's sister mistakes Heathcliff's intensity for a romantic quality. Experience gives her a voice quite different from the sheltered girl's first account of him.

book-madeline-miller-the-song-of-achille.Patroclus: An exiled prince with a healer's temperament. He watches Achilles with the close attention of someone who sees a whole person where others see a legend.
book-madeline-miller-the-song-of-achille.Achilles: A young warrior who makes extraordinary skill look effortless. Alone with Patroclus he has a boy's capacity for play that his public destiny scarcely permits.
book-madeline-miller-the-song-of-achille.Thetis: Achilles's immortal mother takes a long view of her son's glory and a dim view of the mortal boy who loves him.
book-madeline-miller-the-song-of-achille.Briseis: A Trojan captive who learns the Greeks' language and finds a friend in Patroclus. Her wishes count for dangerously little among the men claiming her.
book-madeline-miller-the-song-of-achille.Agamemnon: The Greek commander expects rank to settle every quarrel. His need for a public show of deference puts him on a collision course with Achilles.
book-madeline-miller-the-song-of-achille.Odysseus: The Ithacan king sizes up men quickly and knows which argument each will hear. Wit and calculation give him an edge among stronger warriors.
book-madeline-miller-the-song-of-achille.Hector: Troy's foremost defender bears responsibility for a city and a family. His reputation shadows Achilles long before the two meet in battle.

book-colleen-hoover-it-starts-with-us.Lily Bloom: A florist and new mother negotiating contact with her former husband. A chance encounter with Atlas makes her imagine a relationship she could choose on her own terms.
book-colleen-hoover-it-starts-with-us.Atlas Corrigan: A boy Lily befriended when he was homeless, now a chef. His ability to recognize what somebody needs has outlasted their years apart.
