book-colleen-hoover-it-starts-with-us.Ryle Kincaid: An ambitious neurosurgeon whose attention can feel intoxicating. His tenderness and his capacity for violence leave Lily making decisions he cannot make for her.
book-colleen-hoover-it-starts-with-us.Josh: Atlas's younger half-brother is a wary teenager with a talent for drawing. He wants a say in decisions adults keep making about where he belongs.
book-colleen-hoover-it-starts-with-us.Theo: The young son of Atlas's friend Brad has appointed himself an expert on Atlas's love life. His advice is delivered with magnificent confidence.
book-colleen-hoover-it-starts-with-us.Allysa Kincaid: Ryle's outgoing sister befriends Lily and helps at the flower shop. Loyalty becomes complicated when her friend and her brother need very different things.

book-stephenie-meyer-new-moon.Bella Swan: A teenager newly arrived in rainy Forks who has long been used to looking after a parent. Curiosity takes her closer to danger than caution would allow.
book-stephenie-meyer-new-moon.Jacob Black: A teenage mechanic becomes Bella's closest companion while they restore two motorbikes. A new obligation to his community makes even that easy friendship difficult to explain.
book-stephenie-meyer-new-moon.Edward Cullen: A vampire who hears other people's thoughts. Bella's unreadable mind fascinates him almost as much as her blood, and his self-control is under real strain.
book-stephenie-meyer-new-moon.Alice Cullen: A vampire who glimpses possible futures. She greets Bella with the easy affection of someone who feels their friendship has already happened.
book-stephenie-meyer-new-moon.Aro: An ancient Volturi leader who welcomes visitors with unnerving delight. A touch lets him examine everything that a guest has ever thought.
book-stephenie-meyer-new-moon.Victoria: A watchful vampire with an exceptional instinct for self-preservation. After losing James, she puts that patience to use pursuing a far more personal quarry.
book-stephenie-meyer-new-moon.Sam Uley: A young Quileute pack leader who takes its duty of protection seriously. From outside the pack, his authority over Jacob's friends looks deeply suspicious.

book-aldous-huxley-brave-new-world.Bernard Marx: An Alpha psychologist feels ill at ease in a society engineered for contentment. A sudden taste of popularity tests how much of his objection was to being left out.
book-aldous-huxley-brave-new-world.Lenina Crowne: A conditioning-centre worker enjoys her clothes, friends and prescribed pleasures. John stirs feelings for which she has never needed a vocabulary.
book-aldous-huxley-brave-new-world.John: Raised outside the World State, John learned to name love, humiliation and anger through Shakespeare. His admirers hear a novelty where he means a conviction.
book-aldous-huxley-brave-new-world.Helmholtz Watson: A successful writer of emotional propaganda wants language equal to a genuine difficulty. Popularity has left that particular ambition unsatisfied.
book-aldous-huxley-brave-new-world.Mustapha Mond: A World Controller knows the forbidden books and can explain exactly why he keeps them forbidden. His defence of social stability is disconcertingly articulate.
book-aldous-huxley-brave-new-world.Linda: John's mother was conditioned for one society and stranded in another. Her longing for familiar comforts carries the weight of years of isolation and shame.

book-douglas-adams-the-hitchhikers-guide.Arthur Dent: An Englishman who would like a cup of tea and his house left standing. The destruction of Earth does remarkably little to change the first preference.
book-douglas-adams-the-hitchhikers-guide.Ford Prefect: An alien field researcher who has passed for an out-of-work actor on Earth. He knows where his towel is and roughly how to hitch a lift.
book-douglas-adams-the-hitchhikers-guide.Zaphod Beeblebrox: A two-headed galactic celebrity and politician with an immense appetite for adventure, especially the parts that involve people paying attention to him.
book-douglas-adams-the-hitchhikers-guide.Trillian: A human scientist who took a chance to leave Earth before Arthur did. She is frequently the most technically competent person in an extraordinarily chaotic room.
book-douglas-adams-the-hitchhikers-guide.Marvin: A tremendously intelligent robot with a depressive outlook. Being summoned to open a door is precisely the sort of assignment he has come to expect.
book-douglas-adams-the-hitchhikers-guide.Slartibartfast: A planetary designer proud of the award he won for a coastline. His professional concerns give Arthur a disconcertingly fresh perspective on Earth.

book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Marie-Laure LeBlanc: A blind French girl navigates by counting steps and by handling models her father builds. Shells, stories and radio voices enlarge her sense of place.
book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Werner Pfennig: A German orphan can repair a radio almost by ear. His gift opens doors into an institution whose demands grow harder to reconcile with his conscience.
book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Daniel LeBlanc: The museum locksmith teaches his daughter independence through intricate wooden puzzles. Making a model of a neighbourhood becomes an act of paternal care.
book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Étienne LeBlanc: Marie-Laure's great-uncle is a radio enthusiast living in seclusion after the last war. A child sharing his house gives familiar rooms a new purpose.
book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Reinhold von Rumpel: A German officer appraising confiscated treasures searches for a particular stone. Illness gives the apparent patience of his professional manner an urgent undertow.
book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Jutta Pfennig: Werner's sister listens to distant broadcasts with him and asks what Germany's official voices omit. Her questions stay with him after they are separated.
book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Frank Volkheimer: A physically imposing young soldier protective of Werner. His appreciation of music complicates the frightening impression he makes in uniform.
book-anthony-doerr-all-the-light-we-cann.Madame Manec: Étienne's housekeeper turns domestic competence and neighbourhood friendships toward resistance. People who ignore older women make her work a little easier.

book-stephenie-meyer-eclipse.Bella Swan: A teenager newly arrived in rainy Forks who has long been used to looking after a parent. Curiosity takes her closer to danger than caution would allow.
book-stephenie-meyer-eclipse.Edward Cullen: A vampire who hears other people's thoughts. Bella's unreadable mind fascinates him almost as much as her blood, and his self-control is under real strain.
book-stephenie-meyer-eclipse.Jacob Black: A Quileute teenager who likes repairing engines and makes Bella laugh. His easy company offers her an entry into a community with its own history.
book-stephenie-meyer-eclipse.Victoria: A watchful vampire with an exceptional instinct for self-preservation. After losing James, she puts that patience to use pursuing a far more personal quarry.
book-stephenie-meyer-eclipse.Riley Biers: A newly turned vampire responsible for keeping other newborns in line. His devotion to Victoria makes him susceptible to the story she tells him.
book-stephenie-meyer-eclipse.Rosalie Hale: Edward's adopted sister is protective of the ordinary human future she lost. Bella's willingness to give hers up strikes a particularly painful nerve.
book-stephenie-meyer-eclipse.Jasper Hale: A vampire who senses and influences emotions. His experience with newborn armies gives the Cullens a strategist who understands their enemy from within.

book-sarah-j-maas-crown-of-midnight.Celaena Sardothien (Aelin Galathynius): The king's champion must convince the court she is carrying out orders while deciding in private which commands she can bear to obey.
book-sarah-j-maas-crown-of-midnight.Chaol Westfall: The captain of the royal guard trusts training, order and his oldest friend Dorian. A divided loyalty can unsettle him more than an armed opponent.
book-sarah-j-maas-crown-of-midnight.Dorian Havilliard: Adarlan's crown prince reads voraciously and flirts easily. Behind the good manners is a young man beginning to question the father he will succeed.
book-sarah-j-maas-crown-of-midnight.Nehemia Ytger: A princess of Eyllwe visiting the conquering court. Her apparent ease with ceremony leaves courtiers guessing how much of their conversation she understands.
book-sarah-j-maas-crown-of-midnight.Archer Finn: A celebrated courtesan and an acquaintance from Celaena's past. His clients confide in him, a dangerous advantage in a city full of informants.
book-sarah-j-maas-crown-of-midnight.Roland Havilliard: Dorian's cousin arrives at the glass castle with a polished smile and royal connections. Neither quality tells the prince whose interests he serves.

book-mary-shelley-frankenstein.Victor Frankenstein: A scientist becomes absorbed in the problem of creating life. Once the being looks back at him, intellectual ambition gives way to a failure of care.
book-mary-shelley-frankenstein.Frankenstein’s creature: An abandoned being learns language by observing a household that never sees him. Eloquent appeals for fellowship coexist with fury at repeated rejection.
book-mary-shelley-frankenstein.Elizabeth Lavenza: Victor's beloved is a source of affection and continuity in the Frankenstein household. His secrecy leaves her with little chance to judge danger for herself.
book-mary-shelley-frankenstein.Henry Clerval: Victor's boyhood friend loves literature and travel. He wants to share a sunrise or a good story with a man increasingly absorbed in his own secret labour.
book-mary-shelley-frankenstein.Robert Walton: An Arctic explorer writing to his sister longs for an intellectual equal. Rescuing Victor gives him a friend whose history bears uncomfortably on his own ambition.
book-mary-shelley-frankenstein.Justine Moritz: A young woman taken into the Frankenstein household whose years of loyalty offer little defence against a criminal accusation. Her case puts Victor's silence under pressure.

book-oscar-wilde-the-picture-of-dorian-g.Dorian Gray: A beautiful young man sees his portrait and recoils from the thought of aging. Admiration encourages him to treat experience as something someone else might pay for.
book-oscar-wilde-the-picture-of-dorian-g.Lord Henry Wotton: An aristocratic conversationalist enjoys launching paradoxes and watching them take effect. Dorian proves an audience unusually willing to live out the implications.
book-oscar-wilde-the-picture-of-dorian-g.Basil Hallward: The painter of Dorian's portrait recognizes how much of his own adoration went into the picture. He mistrusts the influence his wittier friend exercises.
book-oscar-wilde-the-picture-of-dorian-g.Sibyl Vane: A young Shakespearean actress can inhabit grand passions onstage. Falling in love in her own life unexpectedly changes what acting means to her.
book-oscar-wilde-the-picture-of-dorian-g.James Vane: Sibyl's sailor brother is protective of her and suspicious of her society admirer. The fact that he knows only a nickname complicates his intentions.

book-sally-rooney-normal-people.Marianne Sheridan: A fiercely intelligent Irish schoolgirl, isolated at school and unsafe at home. University changes her social position faster than it changes how she sees herself.
book-sally-rooney-normal-people.Connell Waldron: A popular school athlete with a private love of literature. He can describe the world beautifully on paper and still fail to say what Marianne needs to hear.
book-sally-rooney-normal-people.Lorraine Waldron: Connell's mother cleans the Sheridans' house and likes Marianne. Her easy moral clarity makes her son's concern about his classmates seem especially small.
book-sally-rooney-normal-people.Alan Sheridan: Marianne's older brother uses the privacy of the family home to intimidate her. His resentment can turn an ordinary exchange into a threat.
book-sally-rooney-normal-people.Denise Sheridan: Marianne's affluent mother is acutely conscious of status. Her willingness to excuse Alan helps determine what her daughter comes to expect from love.
book-sally-rooney-normal-people.Helen Brophy: A medical student who becomes Connell's girlfriend. Their relationship shows him one version of a life that feels socially straightforward.

book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Violet Sorrengail: Violet needs allies beyond Navarre to face a threat its leaders concealed. A young rider trained to remember the official history now has to ask whose accounts are missing.
book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Xaden Riorson: A dragon rider and the son of an executed rebel. As wingleader, he bears responsibility for cadets who share the mark of their parents' rebellion.
book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Ridoc Gamlyn: A quick-witted rider in Violet's squad who uses outrageous jokes to keep his friends talking when fear threatens to silence them.
book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Imogen Cardulo: A pink-haired rider marked by her family's rebellion. She is exacting in training and fiercely protective of the people who have earned her loyalty.
book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Theophanie: A powerful venin with a particular interest in Violet. Her confidence makes an invitation to surrender feel disturbingly personal.
book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Dain Aetos: Violet's childhood friend puts great faith in the riders' rules. His instinct to protect her can make it hard for him to hear what she wants.
book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Tairn: An enormous black dragon with a short temper and a veteran's expectations. His blunt exchanges with Violet have the familiarity of an old argument.
book-rebecca-yarros-onyx-storm.Andarna: A young dragon drawn to Violet. Curiosity gives her questions a directness that can cut straight through the older dragons' solemnity.

book-emily-henry-people-we-meet-on-vacat.Poppy Wright: A travel writer who can make friends almost anywhere. Her favourite part of a decade of glamorous trips is often a running joke with the same companion.
book-emily-henry-people-we-meet-on-vacat.Alex Nilsen: Poppy's reserved best friend is a teacher who likes routine and packing sensibly. On their trips, a dry aside can send her into fits of laughter.
book-emily-henry-people-we-meet-on-vacat.Sarah Torval: A teacher whose relationship with Alex keeps bringing into focus the settled life he might have in their hometown.
book-emily-henry-people-we-meet-on-vacat.Rachel Krohn: Poppy's New York friend, an artist with a social-media following. She is perceptive enough to ask when Poppy last remembers being truly happy.

book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Daisy Jones: A singer and songwriter who believes the whole point of a song is to say exactly what happened. Her lack of a filter is electric onstage and costly off it.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Billy Dunne: The band's driven frontman is trying to protect his sobriety and his marriage. Sharing a microphone with Daisy makes his own lyrics feel newly dangerous.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Camila Dunne: Billy's wife builds a home around a touring musician's absences. Her warmth coexists with a remarkably clear sense of what she will accept.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Karen Sirko: A keyboard player determined to be heard on her own terms. She enjoys belonging to a band and guards the independence it took to get there.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Graham Dunne: Billy's younger brother is the band's guitarist. His affection for Karen forces him to consider whether two people can want different futures and still love each other.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Simone Jackson: A singer carving out a career of her own who offers Daisy the kind of practical loyalty the music business rarely supplies.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Eddie Loving: A guitarist tired of hearing that the band is a democracy while Billy makes the decisions. Years later he can still list the slights.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-daisy-jones-the.Warren Rhodes: The Six's drummer likes playing music, having a good time and letting other people feud. His recollections provide a welcome change of tempo.

book-holly-jackson-a-good-girls-guide-to.Pippa Fitz-Amobi: A meticulous schoolgirl reopens a local murder case for a project. She is good at getting someone talking and much less good at letting a question go.
book-holly-jackson-a-good-girls-guide-to.Ravi Singh: The accused boy's younger brother has lived for years with his town's verdict. He brings personal knowledge and a dry wit to Pip's investigation.
book-holly-jackson-a-good-girls-guide-to.Andie Bell: A popular teenager whose disappearance left behind several versions of the same girl. Pip has to listen for what classmates and adults leave out.
book-holly-jackson-a-good-girls-guide-to.Sal Singh: Ravi's late older brother was blamed for Andie's death. Small memories of his kindness sit uneasily beside the certainty of the town's story.
book-holly-jackson-a-good-girls-guide-to.Cara Ward: Pip's close friend is one of her strongest links to ordinary school life. The case comes dangerously close to the people Cara trusts most.
book-holly-jackson-a-good-girls-guide-to.Elliot Ward: Cara's father is a respected teacher and familiar presence to Pip. Being a trusted adult gives his view of the old case particular weight.

book-andy-weir-project-hail-mary.Ryland Grace: A science teacher wakes on a spacecraft with missing memories. His instinct to design a small experiment becomes both a survival skill and a way to make contact.
book-andy-weir-project-hail-mary.Rocky: An alien engineer whose senses and atmosphere differ radically from Grace's. A shared appetite for making things work gives them a first basis for friendship.
book-andy-weir-project-hail-mary.Eva Stratt: The administrator granted extraordinary powers to save Earth. She treats a scientist's bruised feelings as an acceptable cost if a decision buys the planet time.
book-andy-weir-project-hail-mary.Olesya Ilyukhina: The Russian engineer on the Hail Mary brings technical mastery and irreverent humour to preparations for a mission with grim odds.
book-andy-weir-project-hail-mary.Yáo Li-Jie: The Chinese mission commander is disciplined, composed and clear about what the crew has undertaken. Grace remembers him chiefly through their preparations on Earth.

book-stephenie-meyer-breaking-dawn.Bella Swan: A teenager newly arrived in rainy Forks who has long been used to looking after a parent. Curiosity takes her closer to danger than caution would allow.
book-stephenie-meyer-breaking-dawn.Edward Cullen: A vampire who hears other people's thoughts. Bella's unreadable mind fascinates him almost as much as her blood, and his self-control is under real strain.
book-stephenie-meyer-breaking-dawn.Jacob Black: A Quileute teenager who likes repairing engines and makes Bella laugh. His easy company offers her an entry into a community with its own history.
book-stephenie-meyer-breaking-dawn.Renesmee Cullen: Bella and Edward's fast-growing daughter communicates images and memories by touch. Her direct curiosity complicates every adult effort to keep her a secret.
book-stephenie-meyer-breaking-dawn.Aro: An ancient Volturi leader who welcomes visitors with unnerving delight. A touch lets him examine everything that a guest has ever thought.
book-stephenie-meyer-breaking-dawn.Alice Cullen: A vampire who glimpses possible futures. She greets Bella with the easy affection of someone who feels their friendship has already happened.
book-stephenie-meyer-breaking-dawn.Irina: A member of the Denali coven whose grief over Laurent colours how she sees the Cullens. What she believes she has witnessed carries enormous consequences.

book-bonnie-garmus-lessons-in-chemistry.Elizabeth Zott: A chemist in 1950s California expects evidence to count whoever presents it. On television she addresses home cooks with the same rigour she brings to a lab.
book-bonnie-garmus-lessons-in-chemistry.Calvin Evans: An accomplished research chemist more interested in Elizabeth's ideas than in departmental etiquette. Their scientific collaboration becomes a private language.
book-bonnie-garmus-lessons-in-chemistry.Madeline Zott: Elizabeth's curious young daughter reads far beyond what adults expect. She approaches gaps in her family history as research questions worth pursuing.
book-bonnie-garmus-lessons-in-chemistry.Harriet Sloane: A neighbour who recognizes how much practical support Elizabeth needs. An oppressive marriage has given her very precise ideas about a woman's freedom.
book-bonnie-garmus-lessons-in-chemistry.Walter Pine: A television producer and single father who sees the possibilities of putting Elizabeth on air. He cannot entirely control what she will say there.
book-bonnie-garmus-lessons-in-chemistry.Six-Thirty: Elizabeth's observant dog learns an extraordinary vocabulary. His perspective on a family conversation often differs from what the humans believe they have communicated.
book-bonnie-garmus-lessons-in-chemistry.Don Donatti: A research superior whose authority over jobs and credit exceeds his appetite for original thought. Elizabeth's refusal to flatter him creates a lasting grievance.

book-holly-black-the-cruel-prince.Jude Duarte: A mortal raised among faeries, Jude trains with a sword and learns to exploit her ability to lie. She wants a real share of power at court.
book-holly-black-the-cruel-prince.Cardan Greenbriar: A beautiful, frequently drunk faerie prince who makes a sport of humiliating Jude. His cruelty draws an audience and keeps that audience at a distance.
book-holly-black-the-cruel-prince.Taryn Duarte: Jude's twin thinks a mortal can secure a place in Faerie by learning its rules. The bargains she accepts test the closeness of the sisters.
book-holly-black-the-cruel-prince.Madoc: A redcap general who raises the children of the parents he killed. He teaches Jude strategy with a father's pride and a conqueror's appetite.
book-holly-black-the-cruel-prince.Locke: A faerie courtier who treats other people's attachments as material for an entertaining story. He likes to arrange the scene and watch what follows.
book-holly-black-the-cruel-prince.Balekin Greenbriar: Cardan's elder brother intends to rule. At home he treats punishment as a lesson and obedience as proof that the lesson worked.
book-holly-black-the-cruel-prince.Vivienne: Jude's older half-sister was born faerie and would gladly leave its privileges behind. The ordinary freedoms of the human world mean more to her.

book-khaled-hosseini-a-thousand-splendid.Mariam: Raised outside her wealthy father's legitimate family, Mariam learns early to ration hope. Sharing a household with Laila changes what she is prepared to defend.
book-khaled-hosseini-a-thousand-splendid.Laila: A bright Kabul schoolgirl raised to expect an education. War narrows her choices, but it does little to diminish her capacity to imagine a future.
book-khaled-hosseini-a-thousand-splendid.Rasheed: A Kabul shoemaker who offers security on terms he controls. The difference between his hospitality to a guest and his treatment of a wife is stark.
book-khaled-hosseini-a-thousand-splendid.Tariq: Laila's childhood companion lost a leg to a land mine. His teasing familiarity lets her be an ordinary girl even as their city becomes dangerous.
book-khaled-hosseini-a-thousand-splendid.Jalil: Mariam's prosperous father visits with gifts and stories. She discovers that the warmth of a private visit need not translate into a public acknowledgement.
book-khaled-hosseini-a-thousand-splendid.Nana: Mariam's mother has sharp memories of being cast out. Her warnings can sound cruel to a daughter still hoping to take her father's promises literally.
book-khaled-hosseini-a-thousand-splendid.Aziza: Laila's daughter brings the two women together through the daily work of keeping a child fed, taught and loved in wartime.

book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Celaena Sardothien (Aelin Galathynius): Grief has brought Celaena to Wendlyn. Under Rowan's punishing instruction, recovering her magic means facing parts of her history she has worked hard to bury.
book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Rowan Whitethorn: A Fae warrior sworn to Maeve. As an instructor he has little use for charm, excuses or boasts that somebody cannot back up in the field.
book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Manon Blackbeak: The iron-toothed captain of the Thirteen has been raised to prize obedience and ferocity. Choosing a wyvern tests what she recognizes as strength.
book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Dorian Havilliard: Adarlan's crown prince reads voraciously and flirts easily. Behind the good manners is a young man beginning to question the father he will succeed.
book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Chaol Westfall: The captain of the royal guard trusts training, order and his oldest friend Dorian. A divided loyalty can unsettle him more than an armed opponent.
book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Sorscha: A palace healer whose work brings her close to Dorian. She has survived at court by noticing suffering and attracting very little attention herself.
book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Maeve: A Fae queen accustomed to having warriors kneel when she speaks. She can make a demand sound like the answer to a subject's deepest wish.
book-sarah-j-maas-heir-of-fire.Aedion Ashryver: A general with a reputation for enjoying the conquerors' favour. Any mention of his home, Terrasen, puts a different edge in his voice.

book-ana-huang-twisted-love.Ava Chen: A photography student who looks for beauty as a matter of habit. Recurring gaps in her childhood memories complicate her apparent openness.
book-ana-huang-twisted-love.Alex Volkov: Josh's wealthy, fiercely controlled best friend agrees to look after Ava. He treats nearly every problem as solvable through information, money or leverage.
book-ana-huang-twisted-love.Josh Chen: Ava's protective older brother and an aspiring doctor. Entrusting her to his best friend seems considerably simpler than it turns out to be.
book-ana-huang-twisted-love.Ivan Volkov: Alex's uncle values power, money and the appearance of refinement. Family obligation becomes especially fraught when it overlaps with control of a business.

book-emily-henry-beach-read.January Andrews: A romance novelist trying to write a happy ending after her father's death upends her faith in them. She still has an instinct for a terrific comeback.
book-emily-henry-beach-read.Augustus Everett: A literary novelist with writer's block and a taste for difficult subjects. A genre-swapping bet with his neighbour tests his convictions about happy endings.
book-emily-henry-beach-read.Shadi: January's best friend is an enthusiastic audience for her triumphs and disasters. Their long-distance conversations let January drop the public novelist's voice.
book-emily-henry-beach-read.Sonya: A woman from January's father's Michigan life. She has memories of him that January badly wants to understand and can barely bear to hear.

book-yann-martel-life-of-pi.Piscine Molitor Patel: A zookeeper's son fascinated by animals and several religions. Adrift at sea, he combines a storyteller's imagination with close attention to a predator's habits.
book-yann-martel-life-of-pi.Richard Parker: A Bengal tiger sharing Pi's lifeboat. Space, hunger, scent and territory govern his behaviour and give Pi urgent reasons to keep a daily routine.
book-yann-martel-life-of-pi.Santosh Patel: Pi's practical father runs a zoo and insists his sons understand how dangerous an animal remains, however familiar its face.
book-yann-martel-life-of-pi.Gita Patel: Pi's mother loves books and takes his spiritual curiosity seriously. Her warmth shapes his memories of family life before the voyage.
book-yann-martel-life-of-pi.Ravi Patel: Pi's athletic older brother teases him with the ease of long familiarity. Cricket and sibling jokes belong to the ordinary world Pi remembers.

book-stephen-king-the-shining.Jack Torrance: A recovering alcoholic and aspiring playwright takes a winter caretaking job. He loves his son and fears the anger that has already hurt him.
book-stephen-king-the-shining.Wendy Torrance: Danny's mother wants to believe the family's fresh start will work. She notices danger at the hotel before she can admit what it means for her marriage.
book-stephen-king-the-shining.Danny Torrance: A young boy with an extraordinary sensitivity to other people's thoughts. He often understands that his parents are frightened before he understands the reason.
book-stephen-king-the-shining.Dick Hallorann: The hotel's cook recognizes Danny's psychic gift and gives it a name. His gentle humour puts a frightened child at ease.
book-stephen-king-the-shining.Stuart Ullman: The Overlook's fastidious manager has misgivings about hiring Jack. He presents the hotel's less savoury history as a series of personnel problems.

book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Vera Claythorne: A former governess accepts a secretarial post on an island. Her professional composure starts to fracture around an old memory of a child and the sea.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Philip Lombard: An adventurer who reads physical danger quickly and treats self-preservation as common sense. His candour about past actions is scarcely reassuring.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Lawrence Wargrave: A retired judge listens to the other guests as though they are already in court. He has a practised talent for organizing frightened people.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Edward Armstrong: A successful physician summoned to attend an absent host. The island revives a professional secret he had hoped would remain safely in his past.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.William Blore: A former police inspector arrives under an assumed identity. Investigative experience gives him confidence, sometimes well beyond what his deductions deserve.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Emily Brent: A devout older woman whose certainty about sin leaves little room for mercy. She considers her conscience entirely clear.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.John Macarthur: A retired general recognizes an accusation that nobody else should know about. He responds to the island's growing menace with an unsettling resignation.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Anthony Marston: A wealthy young motorist treats speed and risk as pleasures. He is much less interested in the people who bear the consequences.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Thomas Rogers: The newly hired butler keeps serving meals and announcing guests even as the apparent rules of the household disintegrate.
book-agatha-christie-and-then-there-were.Ethel Rogers: The housekeeper arrives with her husband to staff an unfamiliar house. Hearing the accusation against them visibly shakes her more than it shakes him.

book-frank-herbert-dune.Paul Atreides: The young Atreides heir has been trained by warriors, strategists and his Bene Gesserit mother. His dreams of Arrakis feel disturbingly like memories.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Lady Jessica: A Bene Gesserit adept and Paul's mother, Jessica reads a shift in breathing as readily as speech. Loyalty to her order competes with love for her family.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Duke Leto Atreides: Paul's father accepts rule of a desert planet knowing the appointment may be a trap. He earns loyalty by treating his people's lives as his responsibility.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Chani: A young Fremen woman at ease in terrain that terrifies the newcomers. Paul encounters her in dreams before he understands her place in the desert.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Stilgar: A Fremen leader who measures authority by what keeps the sietch alive. Outsiders earn his attention by learning what water actually costs.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Baron Vladimir Harkonnen: The Harkonnen patriarch treats family members and captured territories as pieces in a long political calculation. He enjoys explaining a trap to a captive audience.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Feyd-Rautha Harkonnen: The Baron's ambitious young nephew combines a fighter's skill with a taste for spectacle. The arena lets him practise both before a crowd.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Gurney Halleck: An Atreides weapons master who sings and plays the baliset. He can turn a training bout deadly serious without losing his taste for a verse.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Duncan Idaho: A swordmaster sent among the Fremen because he can earn the respect of strangers. His loyalty to House Atreides is personal.
book-frank-herbert-dune.Liet-Kynes: An imperial ecologist who moves between official duties and Fremen society. The apparently barren planet looks quite different through his eyes.

book-emily-henry-book-lovers.Nora Stephens: A fiercely effective literary agent who handles emergencies for her clients and younger sister. Being cast as the cold career woman in somebody else's romance rankles.
book-emily-henry-book-lovers.Charlie Lastra: A demanding editor with a famously exacting eye. He and Nora can conduct a flirtation almost entirely through a disagreement about a manuscript.
book-emily-henry-book-lovers.Libby Stephens: Nora's younger sister plans a small-town holiday with a checklist of romantic adventures. Beneath the enthusiasm, she has reasons of her own for arranging the trip.
book-emily-henry-book-lovers.Dusty Fielding: A successful novelist represented by Nora. Her fiction made Sunshine Falls famous, and her newest manuscript gives her agent an unexpectedly personal editorial problem.

book-s-e-hinton-the-outsiders.Ponyboy Curtis: A young Greaser who reads poetry and watches sunsets. His first-person voice lets tenderness show through the tough language expected of his gang.
book-s-e-hinton-the-outsiders.Johnny Cade: A frightened, watchful boy who finds more safety with the gang than at home. His devotion to Ponyboy can make him unexpectedly decisive.
book-s-e-hinton-the-outsiders.Dallas Winston: A streetwise older Greaser cultivates indifference to almost everything. His fierce attachment to Johnny is the conspicuous exception.
book-s-e-hinton-the-outsiders.Sodapop Curtis: Ponyboy's outgoing middle brother works at a filling station and tries to mediate at home. His easy charm conceals how hard their quarrels land.
book-s-e-hinton-the-outsiders.Darrel Curtis: The eldest Curtis brother has traded his own plans for the work of keeping the boys together. His fear for Ponyboy often comes out as anger.
book-s-e-hinton-the-outsiders.Cherry Valance: A Soc girl who talks to Ponyboy about sunsets and class loyalties. Sympathy across the divide does not erase the life she returns to afterward.
book-s-e-hinton-the-outsiders.Two-Bit Mathews: The gang's resident joker likes switchblades, shoplifting and an audience. His comic timing is part of the way he keeps younger friends close.

book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Celaena Sardothien (Aelin Galathynius): Back in Rifthold, Celaena has old debts to settle. The skills that kept one assassin alive must now protect people counting on a queen.
book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Aedion Ashryver: A general with a reputation for enjoying the conquerors' favour. Any mention of his home, Terrasen, puts a different edge in his voice.
book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Lysandra: A courtesan who learned early to become whatever a client wanted to see. Her protectiveness toward young Evangeline reveals a more enduring loyalty.
book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Manon Blackbeak: The iron-toothed captain of the Thirteen has been raised to prize obedience and ferocity. Choosing a wyvern tests what she recognizes as strength.
book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Dorian Havilliard: Adarlan's crown prince reads voraciously and flirts easily. Behind the good manners is a young man beginning to question the father he will succeed.
book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Rowan Whitethorn: A Fae warrior sworn to Maeve. As an instructor he has little use for charm, excuses or boasts that somebody cannot back up in the field.
book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Arobynn Hamel: The wealthy master of the Assassins' Guild once trained Celaena. He remembers the cost of every favour he has ever done her.
book-sarah-j-maas-queen-of-shadows.Chaol Westfall: The captain of the royal guard trusts training, order and his oldest friend Dorian. A divided loyalty can unsettle him more than an armed opponent.

book-v-e-schwab-the-invisible-life-of-ad.Addie LaRue: A young Frenchwoman bargains for freedom and finds herself forgotten by everyone she meets. She learns to leave traces through other people's art.
book-v-e-schwab-the-invisible-life-of-ad.Henry Strauss: A bookseller who, impossibly, remembers Addie. His sensitivity to other people's expectations makes being truly seen an especially complicated gift.
book-v-e-schwab-the-invisible-life-of-ad.Luc: The darkness that accepted Addie's bargain takes a familiar human shape. He has centuries to wait and treats conversation as part of the contest.
book-v-e-schwab-the-invisible-life-of-ad.Bea: Henry's art-minded friend takes images and ideas seriously. Her eye for connections gives Addie a rare way to see the marks she has left.
book-v-e-schwab-the-invisible-life-of-ad.Robbie: Henry's friend and former lover is an actor whose warmth comes with an acute need for acknowledgement. Addie's curse makes introductions especially awkward.

book-bram-stoker-dracula.Count Dracula: A Transylvanian aristocrat welcomes a young English solicitor with elaborate courtesy. His study of timetables, pronunciation and property gives predation a chilling practicality.
book-bram-stoker-dracula.Mina Harker: A teacher skilled in shorthand and typing turns scattered accounts into evidence the group can use. Her gift is seeing what one witness alone cannot.
book-bram-stoker-dracula.Jonathan Harker: A solicitor goes abroad to arrange a property transaction. Professional politeness keeps him at the dinner table long after he begins to suspect he is a prisoner.
book-bram-stoker-dracula.Abraham Van Helsing: A Dutch physician whose wide reading lets him entertain explanations his colleagues dismiss. He has to turn a collection of grieving friends into collaborators.
book-bram-stoker-dracula.Lucy Westenra: Mina's affectionate friend handles three suitors with surprising kindness. Her unexplained illness brings people of sharply different temperaments to the same bedside.
book-bram-stoker-dracula.John Seward: A young asylum doctor records observations on a phonograph. His disciplined interest in unusual behaviour turns personal when Lucy begins to decline.
book-bram-stoker-dracula.Renfield: Seward's patient connects flies, spiders and birds through a theory about accumulating life. His periods of lucidity make his warnings difficult to dismiss.

book-emily-henry-happy-place.Harriet Kilpatrick: A surgical resident who tries to keep the peace even when it means concealing a breakup. Her closest friends know her laugh better than her doubts.
book-emily-henry-happy-place.Wyn Connor: Harriet's former fiancé can make an entire group feel at ease. Saying exactly what he wants for his own future is considerably harder.
book-emily-henry-happy-place.Sabrina Armas: The friend who gathers everyone at her family's Maine cottage. She builds traditions with the determination of someone who knows they can end.
book-emily-henry-happy-place.Cleo James: An artist and grower whose quiet companionship has anchored the friend group since college. She notices when the old routine stops fitting.
book-emily-henry-happy-place.Parth Nayak: Sabrina's outgoing partner knows how to make a gathering feel like a celebration. He shares her attachment to the friendships formed around the cottage.
book-emily-henry-happy-place.Kim Carmichael: Cleo's exuberant partner brings fresh energy to an established circle. Her open affection makes the group's carefully guarded secrets particularly conspicuous.

book-franz-kafka-the-metamorphosis.Gregor Samsa: A travelling salesman wakes in an insectlike body and worries first about missing his train. He understands his family's speech long after they stop understanding his.
book-franz-kafka-the-metamorphosis.Grete Samsa: Gregor's younger sister experiments with food and makes room for him to crawl. As care becomes her daily responsibility, her way of speaking about her brother changes.
book-franz-kafka-the-metamorphosis.Mr. Samsa: Gregor's father has relied on his son's wages. The family crisis returns him to paid work and gives his old authority a startling new physical force.
book-franz-kafka-the-metamorphosis.Mrs. Samsa: Gregor's mother wants to see the son she remembers and struggles to bear the sight of his changed form. Affection and fright pull her in opposite directions.

book-madeline-miller-circe.Circe: A daughter of the sun god with an unimpressive voice by divine standards. Alone on her island, she develops her witchcraft through stubborn experiment.
book-madeline-miller-circe.Helios: The sun god rules a glittering household where rank determines whose feelings matter. His daughter's defiance registers first as an affront to his authority.
book-madeline-miller-circe.Pasiphaë: Circe's sister, the queen of Crete, turns divine beauty and bitter intelligence to her own purposes. Asking Circe for help scarcely softens their rivalry.
book-madeline-miller-circe.Scylla: A beautiful nymph whose encounter with Circe sets a terrible transformation in motion. Her presence makes jealousy something more dangerous than a passing feeling.
book-madeline-miller-circe.Odysseus: A shipwrecked king who can hold Circe's attention with a story. His charm leaves open the question of how faithfully he tells it.
book-madeline-miller-circe.Telegonus: Circe's son grows up on an island listening to stories about his absent father. His longing for the world tests the limits of his mother's protection.
book-madeline-miller-circe.Penelope: Odysseus's wife has spent years keeping a household together under siege by suitors. She watches before speaking and knows the uses of a delay.
book-madeline-miller-circe.Telemachus: Penelope's son carries the burden of a famous father without sharing his appetite for glory. His steadiness unsettles some of Circe's expectations.

book-e-lockhart-we-were-liars.Cadence Sinclair Eastman: The eldest Sinclair grandchild tries to reconstruct a summer she can barely remember. Her sharp observations arrive in fragments as she works through pain.
book-e-lockhart-we-were-liars.Gat Patil: A thoughtful outsider in the Sinclair family's island circle. He asks questions about privilege that the cousins have learned to glide past.
book-e-lockhart-we-were-liars.Mirren Sheffield: Cadence's cousin enjoys the children's private island world while also feeling the expectations placed on the Sinclair girls.
book-e-lockhart-we-were-liars.Johnny Dennis: Cadence's cousin brings mischief and reckless energy to the little group. With Gat beside him he can briefly ignore the adults' dynastic manoeuvring.
book-e-lockhart-we-were-liars.Harris Sinclair: The wealthy patriarch owns the island his family returns to every summer. Even small signs of his approval set his daughters competing.

book-gabrielle-zevin-tomorrow-and-tomorr.Sam Masur: A game designer living with chronic pain finds ease in invented worlds and in playing with Sadie. Making a game together is riskier than playing one.
book-gabrielle-zevin-tomorrow-and-tomorr.Sadie Green: A gifted programmer wants her work recognized as art. Collaborating with Sam exposes the gap between doing creative labour and receiving public credit for it.
book-gabrielle-zevin-tomorrow-and-tomorr.Marx Watanabe: Sam's generous college roommate becomes the producer who makes collaboration possible. He is often translating between two people convinced they already understand each other.
book-gabrielle-zevin-tomorrow-and-tomorr.Dov Mizrah: A celebrated game designer and Sadie's teacher whose professional encouragement comes with intimate demands. His influence follows her beyond the classroom.
book-gabrielle-zevin-tomorrow-and-tomorr.Anna Lee: Sam's mother is an actress whose life moves between New York and Los Angeles. His memories preserve her humour as well as the circumstances of her loss.
book-gabrielle-zevin-tomorrow-and-tomorr.Zoe Cadogan: A composer in Marx's circle brings music to the collaborators' work. Her confidence about intimacy and friendship opens possibilities the others tend to overthink.

book-emily-henry-funny-story.Daphne Vincent: A children's librarian stranded in her ex-fiancé's hometown. Story time comes naturally, while explaining how she ended up living with Miles takes considerably longer.
book-emily-henry-funny-story.Miles Nowak: Petra's ex is a laid-back bartender who knows everyone in town. His generosity makes Daphne wonder how a man with so many friends came to feel disposable.
book-emily-henry-funny-story.Peter Collins: Daphne's meticulously organized former fiancé has a polished explanation for leaving her. He expects the people affected to accept his version with good grace.
book-emily-henry-funny-story.Petra Comer: Peter's childhood best friend, whose sudden relationship with him upends two households. To Daphne, she initially seems to have walked off with an entire life.
book-emily-henry-funny-story.Ashleigh: Daphne's co-worker at the library is blunt, funny and open to a friendship negotiated on terms that suit them both.

book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Celaena Sardothien (Aelin Galathynius): Terrasen's queen needs ships, allies and a country prepared to receive her. Her habit of keeping plans secret comes at a cost among friends.
book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Rowan Whitethorn: A Fae warrior sworn to Maeve. As an instructor he has little use for charm, excuses or boasts that somebody cannot back up in the field.
book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Manon Blackbeak: The iron-toothed captain of the Thirteen has been raised to prize obedience and ferocity. Choosing a wyvern tests what she recognizes as strength.
book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Elide Lochan: A young noblewoman raised in captivity who survives by reading other people's intentions. She is very good at letting a captor believe a lie was his idea.
book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Lorcan Salvaterre: Maeve's formidable demi-Fae warrior is used to solitude and swift obedience. Travelling with Elide requires a different sort of attention.
book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Lysandra: A courtesan who learned early to become whatever a client wanted to see. Her protectiveness toward young Evangeline reveals a more enduring loyalty.
book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Dorian Havilliard: Adarlan's crown prince reads voraciously and flirts easily. Behind the good manners is a young man beginning to question the father he will succeed.
book-sarah-j-maas-empire-of-storms.Maeve: A Fae queen accustomed to having warriors kneel when she speaks. She can make a demand sound like the answer to a subject's deepest wish.

book-hannah-grace-icebreaker.Anastasia Allen: A pairs skater with a meticulously scheduled life and Olympic ambitions. Sharing ice with the hockey team threatens the control she relies on to compete.
book-hannah-grace-icebreaker.Nathan Hawkins: The Maple Hills hockey captain takes his responsibilities personally. With Anastasia, patience and a willingness to learn on unfamiliar ice work better than bravado.
book-hannah-grace-icebreaker.Aaron Carlisle: Anastasia's longtime skating partner expects her to arrange her training and personal life around their joint ambitions. His approval can vanish without warning.
book-hannah-grace-icebreaker.Lola Mitchell: Anastasia's outspoken roommate studies theatre and takes friendship seriously. She has few reservations about nudging her friend into the hockey team's social orbit.
book-hannah-grace-icebreaker.Robbie Hamlet: A hockey coach and close friend of Nathan's. His relationship with Lola gives the rival groups sharing the rink another reason to spend time together.

book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-earth-and-blo.Bryce Quinlan: A half-Fae gallery employee with a dancer's feet and a party girl's reputation. Jokes come easily, especially when somebody gets close to her grief.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-earth-and-blo.Hunt Athalar: An enslaved angel and highly trained killer. Away from orders and surveillance, he would happily spend an afternoon watching sunball on the couch.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-earth-and-blo.Danika Fendyr: Bryce's closest friend leads a pack of wolf shifters. She can fill a nightclub with laughter and have her wolves in formation a moment later.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-earth-and-blo.Ruhn Danaan: A Fae crown prince with a lip ring, a chosen family of friends and a prickly tenderness for his half-sister Bryce.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-earth-and-blo.Lehabah: A tiny fire sprite who watches over the gallery's underground library. She adores television dramas and takes her friendships just as seriously.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-earth-and-blo.Micah Domitus: The archangel governing Crescent City expects both the police and his personal enforcers to answer to him. He seldom needs to raise his voice.

book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Haymitch Abernathy: A sixteen-year-old from the Seam who would rather spend his birthday with Lenore Dove. Chosen for the Quarter Quell, he starts noticing who arranges every camera shot.
book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Lenore Dove Baird: A young Covey woman and Haymitch's sweetheart. She asks questions about the Capitol that are dangerous even when spoken in private.
book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Maysilee Donner: The daughter of a District 12 shopkeeper brings sharp manners and a sharper tongue to the Quell. Haymitch has to revise his first impression of her.
book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Louella McCoy: A young girl from the Seam whom Haymitch has known since childhood. Their familiarity offers a little comfort amid the spectacle of the reaping.
book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Wyatt Callow: A District 12 tribute from a family of bookmakers who can work out the odds faster than most people can frame the question.
book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Plutarch Heavensbee: A young Capitol cameraman covering the reaping in District 12. He knows how a change of angle can turn a dangerous incident into an acceptable broadcast.
book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Coriolanus Snow: Panem's president speaks quietly, prizes order and takes a personal interest in anyone capable of moving a crowd. His visits are heralded by white roses.
book-suzanne-collins-sunrise-on-the-reap.Lou Lou: A frightened girl thrust into the Capitol's presentation of District 12. Haymitch must negotiate the distance between the story on camera and the child before him.

book-andy-weir-the-martian.Mark Watney: A botanist and engineer stranded on Mars. His log swings between bad jokes and exact arithmetic because the difference between two numbers can mean another meal.
book-andy-weir-the-martian.Melissa Lewis: The Ares mission commander is a geologist who loves disco. Her trained decisiveness is tested by the consequences of a decision made in a storm.
book-andy-weir-the-martian.Mitch Henderson: The flight director sees the astronauts as colleagues entitled to make choices about their own risks. That conviction puts him at odds with NASA leadership.
book-andy-weir-the-martian.Venkat Kapoor: NASA's Mars operations director must turn a planetful of ingenious suggestions into a feasible rescue. He keeps asking what each proposal will cost in time.
book-andy-weir-the-martian.Annie Montrose: NASA's public-relations chief fields questions from the world while privately demanding straight answers from her colleagues. Her language gets considerably saltier off camera.
book-andy-weir-the-martian.Beth Johanssen: The crew's computer specialist works through technical failures with quiet concentration. She finds companionship in a crew that has become her whole immediate world.
book-andy-weir-the-martian.Rich Purnell: An astrodynamicist so absorbed in an orbital solution that workplace protocol barely registers. He can make an outrageous trajectory intelligible with a simple demonstration.

book-taylor-jenkins-reid-malibu-rising.Nina Riva: The eldest Riva child is a surfer and model who has spent so long taking care of her siblings that nobody remembers to ask what she wants.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-malibu-rising.Jay Riva: A championship surfer whose identity depends on what his body can do. His brother Hud knows the pressure of that life unusually well.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-malibu-rising.Hud Riva: A photographer accustomed to watching his brother through a lens. He is tender with people he loves and anxious about a secret that could hurt Jay.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-malibu-rising.Kit Riva: The youngest Riva sibling has genuine talent on a surfboard. Being treated as everybody's kid sister is starting to wear thin.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-malibu-rising.Mick Riva: A star singer whose charisma repeatedly persuades people to forgive his absences. His children have had far more practice living without him.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-malibu-rising.June Riva: The Riva children's mother runs the family restaurant. Her enduring love for Mick exists alongside the daily practical burden of his leaving.

book-colleen-hoover-november-9.Fallon O’Neil: A young actress whose career changed after a fire. She agrees to meet Ben once a year, giving both of them time to build lives between encounters.
book-colleen-hoover-november-9.Benton James Kessler: An aspiring novelist intrigued by Fallon's story. Having a writer's instinct for shaping a scene becomes dangerous when the scene belongs to someone he loves.
book-colleen-hoover-november-9.Donovan O’Neil: Fallon's father is a former actor with firm ideas about how his daughter looks and what those looks mean for a career.
book-colleen-hoover-november-9.Jordyn Kessler: Ben's sister-in-law is woven into his family's daily life. Responsibilities to her complicate what he can promise Fallon on their yearly meetings.

book-sue-monk-kidd-the-secret-life-of-be.Lily Owens: A white South Carolina teenager searching for the truth about her mother finds shelter with sisters who keep bees. She is an inventive, not always reliable guest.
book-sue-monk-kidd-the-secret-life-of-be.Rosaleen Daise: The Black woman who has cared for Lily insists on her own right to register to vote. Her independence exceeds Lily's understanding of their relationship.
book-sue-monk-kidd-the-secret-life-of-be.August Boatwright: A beekeeper who invites Lily into her honey house. Her patient instruction in handling a hive also teaches a newcomer how to pay attention.
book-sue-monk-kidd-the-secret-life-of-be.June Boatwright: August's sister is a cellist with a guarded response to Lily's arrival. Protecting her household matters more to her than putting a stranger at ease.
book-sue-monk-kidd-the-secret-life-of-be.May Boatwright: A Boatwright sister who feels other people's suffering with extraordinary intensity. A wall in the garden gives her grief a physical place.
book-sue-monk-kidd-the-secret-life-of-be.T. Ray Owens: Lily's father runs a peach farm and rules the household through anger. What he says about Lily's mother has shaped the girl's sense of herself.
book-sue-monk-kidd-the-secret-life-of-be.Zachary Taylor: A young Black beekeeper with ambitions to become a lawyer. Working alongside Lily opens a friendship exposed to dangers she is only starting to grasp.

book-jane-austen-sense-and-sensibility.Elinor Dashwood: The eldest Dashwood sister manages the household's changed circumstances with tact. Keeping confidences becomes especially hard when nobody realizes she needs comfort herself.
book-jane-austen-sense-and-sensibility.Marianne Dashwood: Elinor's younger sister believes genuine feeling ought to be fully expressed. She hears a shared taste in poetry or music as a promise about character.
book-jane-austen-sense-and-sensibility.Edward Ferrars: A reserved young man who would rather live quietly than fulfil his family's social ambitions. An old obligation severely limits what he can say to Elinor.
book-jane-austen-sense-and-sensibility.Colonel Brandon: A steady, observant former soldier whose attachment to Marianne develops without any expectation that she will consider him a romantic figure.
book-jane-austen-sense-and-sensibility.John Willoughby: A handsome neighbour who rescues Marianne in a rainstorm and eagerly shares her enthusiasms. His reluctance to define their understanding leaves her dangerously exposed.
book-jane-austen-sense-and-sensibility.Lucy Steele: A young woman without money or powerful connections who understands the strategic value of a confidence. She chooses Elinor as a listener with considerable deliberation.

book-mark-twain-adventures-of-huckleberr.Huckleberry Finn: A boy travelling down the Mississippi has learned society's rules well enough to feel guilty when his own judgment is more humane than theirs.
book-mark-twain-adventures-of-huckleberr.Jim: An enslaved man seizes a chance for freedom and hopes to reunite his family. His care for Huck makes their raft a place of mutual dependence.
book-mark-twain-adventures-of-huckleberr.Tom Sawyer: Huck's imaginative friend loves a complicated adventure patterned on his reading. The fact that other people must bear the consequences rarely enters the plan.
book-mark-twain-adventures-of-huckleberr.Pap Finn: Huck's violent father resents his son's education and sees the boy's money as paternal property. His reappearance makes flight an immediate necessity.
book-mark-twain-adventures-of-huckleberr.The Duke: A travelling confidence man invents an aristocratic identity and profitable entertainments. His audiences' desire to appear sophisticated is one of his most reliable assets.
book-mark-twain-adventures-of-huckleberr.The King: The older swindler on the raft can become a preacher, an heir or a dispossessed monarch between towns. He spots opportunities even his partner finds distasteful.

book-suzanne-collins-the-ballad-of-songb.Coriolanus Snow: An eighteen-year-old Capitol student conceals his family's poverty beneath a carefully tended shirt. Mentoring Lucy Gray could win him the future he thinks his name deserves.
book-suzanne-collins-the-ballad-of-songb.Lucy Gray Baird: A travelling performer's daughter who steps onto the reaping stage and sings. She is an expert at winning over a crowd while keeping her own counsel.
book-suzanne-collins-the-ballad-of-songb.Sejanus Plinth: A district-born student whose father's fortune bought the family a place in the Capitol. He still recognizes the tributes as people he might have known.
book-suzanne-collins-the-ballad-of-songb.Volumnia Gaul: The Head Gamemaker is a scientist with a taste for alarming demonstrations. Her sing-song questions invite students to discover how far they will go to please her.
book-suzanne-collins-the-ballad-of-songb.Casca Highbottom: The dean credited with inventing the Games carries that distinction with visible distaste. He has a particular interest in young Coriolanus Snow.
book-suzanne-collins-the-ballad-of-songb.Tigris Snow: Coriolanus's cousin is a gifted seamstress keeping a threadbare household presentable. She also listens when he confesses things he could never tell their grandmother.
book-suzanne-collins-the-ballad-of-songb.Reaper Ash: A physically imposing District 11 tribute who regards the Capitol with open contempt. His sense of dignity extends to the people the Games ask him to kill.

book-stephen-king-it.Bill Denbrough: A boy with a stutter and a storyteller's imagination. Grief for his little brother drives him to investigate what the adults of Derry overlook.
book-stephen-king-it.Beverly Marsh: The only girl in the Losers' Club is a superb shot. Her friends offer a freedom and safety she rarely feels at home.
book-stephen-king-it.Ben Hanscom: A lonely newcomer who likes libraries and understands how things fit together. He expresses feelings he cannot say aloud in a poem.
book-stephen-king-it.Richie Tozier: A quick-witted boy who cycles through comic voices, particularly when frightened. Keeping his friends laughing is one way he takes care of them.
book-stephen-king-it.Eddie Kaspbrak: A cautious child raised to fear sickness and injury. Friendship gives him reasons to test the limits his mother has set for him.
book-stephen-king-it.Mike Hanlon: A Black boy from a family with deep local knowledge. His interest in Derry's buried history gives the friends a memory larger than their own.
book-stephen-king-it.Stanley Uris: A birdwatcher who loves the orderly precision of identifying a species. What he sees in Derry threatens his trust that the world can be classified.
book-stephen-king-it.Pennywise: A predator that wears a clown's face and adapts its appearance to a child's fear. The friendly greeting should almost work.
book-stephen-king-it.Henry Bowers: A local bully whose home life fuels his rage. With younger boys watching him, every perceived slight becomes a test of dominance.

book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Celaena Sardothien (Aelin Galathynius): Cut off from the people depending on her, Aelin has to find a way to endure captivity while others fight for Terrasen in her name.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Rowan Whitethorn: A Fae warrior sworn to Maeve. As an instructor he has little use for charm, excuses or boasts that somebody cannot back up in the field.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Manon Blackbeak: The iron-toothed captain of the Thirteen has been raised to prize obedience and ferocity. Choosing a wyvern tests what she recognizes as strength.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Dorian Havilliard: Adarlan's crown prince reads voraciously and flirts easily. Behind the good manners is a young man beginning to question the father he will succeed.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Yrene Towers: A gifted healer at the Torre Cesme. She can hold compassion for an injured man and anger at the uniform he wore in the same conversation.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Aedion Ashryver: A general with a reputation for enjoying the conquerors' favour. Any mention of his home, Terrasen, puts a different edge in his voice.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Lysandra: A courtesan who learned early to become whatever a client wanted to see. Her protectiveness toward young Evangeline reveals a more enduring loyalty.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Maeve: A Fae queen accustomed to having warriors kneel when she speaks. She can make a demand sound like the answer to a subject's deepest wish.
book-sarah-j-maas-kingdom-of-ash.Erawan: A Valg king who regards human bodies as both vessels and resources. His calm interest in a person's gifts can be more frightening than rage.

book-fredrik-backman-a-man-called-ove.Ove: A widower who enforces the neighbourhood rules and has firm views on how to park a trailer. He keeps helping people even while complaining about them.
book-fredrik-backman-a-man-called-ove.Parvaneh: Ove's pregnant new neighbour is unmoved by his attempts to be left alone. She recognizes competence, loneliness and a potential driving instructor in the same man.
book-fredrik-backman-a-man-called-ove.Sonja: Ove's late wife was a teacher who loved colour and conversation. His memories of her explain much that his neighbours find inexplicable.
book-fredrik-backman-a-man-called-ove.Rune: Ove's old friend and rival shares his devotion to the neighbourhood, although differences in car preference have been known to strain the friendship.
book-fredrik-backman-a-man-called-ove.Anita: Rune's wife needs help caring for her husband. Her predicament gives Ove's old quarrels a very different scale.
book-fredrik-backman-a-man-called-ove.Patrick: Parvaneh's husband makes an unfortunate first impression while parking a trailer. His friendliness survives a fair amount of instruction from next door.

book-casey-mcquiston-red-white-royal-blu.Alex Claremont-Diaz: The US president's son approaches politics like an ambitious young campaigner. His competitive banter with a British prince starts to sound remarkably like flirting.
book-casey-mcquiston-red-white-royal-blu.Prince Henry: A British prince trained to keep his face composed in every photograph. In his correspondence with Alex he can finally use his own voice.
book-casey-mcquiston-red-white-royal-blu.Zahra Bankston: The president's deputy chief of staff handles family emergencies with a campaign professional's ferocious efficiency. Alex creates employment enough for several people.
book-casey-mcquiston-red-white-royal-blu.Nora Holleran: The vice president's granddaughter is a gifted analyst and one of Alex's closest friends. She reads his patterns almost as readily as polling data.
book-casey-mcquiston-red-white-royal-blu.June Claremont-Diaz: Alex's journalist sister is protective of her brother and wary of being absorbed into a political brand. She would like to write her own story.
book-casey-mcquiston-red-white-royal-blu.Ellen Claremont: The first woman to become US president is also Alex's mother. Supporting her son can mean planning carefully for the political consequences of his private happiness.

book-gillian-flynn-sharp-objects.Camille Preaker: A reporter returns to her Missouri hometown to investigate murdered girls. At her mother's table, the veteran journalist can feel like a powerless daughter again.
book-gillian-flynn-sharp-objects.Adora Crellin: Camille's mother presides over her household and the town's social order. She presents control as a delicate form of maternal concern.
book-gillian-flynn-sharp-objects.Amma Crellin: Camille's teenage half-sister changes manner between her mother's rooms and the town's streets. She is adept at letting each audience see a different girl.
book-gillian-flynn-sharp-objects.Richard Willis: An outsider detective investigating the killings. He and Camille trade local knowledge and professional curiosity without quite settling whether they can trust each other.
book-gillian-flynn-sharp-objects.Alan Crellin: Adora's husband maintains a carefully insulated domestic life. His loyalty to his wife often takes the form of declining to notice.

book-sarah-j-maas-tower-of-dawn.Chaol Westfall: The captain of the royal guard trusts training, order and his oldest friend Dorian. A divided loyalty can unsettle him more than an armed opponent.
book-sarah-j-maas-tower-of-dawn.Yrene Towers: A gifted healer at the Torre Cesme. She can hold compassion for an injured man and anger at the uniform he wore in the same conversation.
book-sarah-j-maas-tower-of-dawn.Nesryn Faliq: An archer from Adarlan whose family roots lie in the southern continent. Returning there lets her explore a life beyond serving another country's crown.
book-sarah-j-maas-tower-of-dawn.Sartaq: A southern prince more at home among the great birds and riders of his rukhin than at a formal gathering of potential heirs.
book-sarah-j-maas-tower-of-dawn.Hasar: A sharp-tongued princess of the southern empire who makes conversation into a test. Her warmth toward her companions can be entirely genuine.
book-sarah-j-maas-tower-of-dawn.Duva: The khagan's pregnant daughter appears content with her husband and a quieter place in a family crowded with contenders for power.

book-abby-jimenez-just-for-the-summer.Emma Grant: A travelling nurse accustomed to packing lightly and keeping emotional exits open. Her instinct to give her mother another chance runs deeper than she admits.
book-abby-jimenez-just-for-the-summer.Justin Dahl: A man who jokes online about his dating curse while facing serious new family responsibilities. He shows affection through plans worked out in advance.
book-abby-jimenez-just-for-the-summer.Maddy: Emma's best friend, foster sister and fellow travelling nurse. Years of watching Emma forgive her mother have made Maddy a fiercely protective travelling companion.
book-abby-jimenez-just-for-the-summer.Amber: Emma's unpredictable mother can make a reunion feel like the beginning of a better life. Her daughter has learned to hope for that beginning many times.

book-leigh-bardugo-six-of-crows.Kaz Brekker: A teenage gang leader who walks with a cane and charges for favours. His plans allow for almost everything except having to admit he needs somebody.
book-leigh-bardugo-six-of-crows.Inej Ghafa: An acrobat turned spy who moves across Ketterdam's rooftops in near silence. Her blades bear saints' names, and her faith shapes what jobs she will take.
book-leigh-bardugo-six-of-crows.Jesper Fahey: A sharpshooter who can hit almost anything and finds it nearly impossible to leave a gambling table. His jokes speed up when the odds turn ugly.
book-leigh-bardugo-six-of-crows.Nina Zenik: A Grisha Heartrender with a gift for languages, a taste for waffles and an inconvenient capacity to care for somebody raised to hate her.
book-leigh-bardugo-six-of-crows.Matthias Helvar: A Fjerdan soldier trained to hunt Grisha. His rigid sense of honour becomes painful when his own experience contradicts what he was taught.
book-leigh-bardugo-six-of-crows.Wylan Van Eck: A merchant's son with a musician's ear and a knack for explosives. Kaz's crew keeps discovering things his powerful father failed to value.
book-leigh-bardugo-six-of-crows.Jan Van Eck: A prosperous merchant who puts contracts, reputation and return on investment above almost everything. He brings the same accounting to his relationship with his son.

book-christina-lauren-the-unhoneymooners.Olive Torres: An unemployed woman who considers herself chronically unlucky suddenly inherits her twin's Hawaiian honeymoon, along with a travel companion she can barely stand.
book-christina-lauren-the-unhoneymooners.Ethan Thomas: The groom's brother is equally unenthusiastic about impersonating Olive's husband. Away from family gatherings, his dry humour starts to land differently.
book-christina-lauren-the-unhoneymooners.Ami Torres: Olive's twin built an entire wedding out of contests and giveaways. She lends her sister the honeymoon when illness takes out the wedding party.
book-christina-lauren-the-unhoneymooners.Dane Thomas: Ami's groom and Ethan's brother enjoys being liked. Two people comparing notes about his behaviour could threaten the version of himself each family knows.

book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Claire Fraser: A wartime nurse displaced from the twentieth century into the Scottish Highlands. Clinical confidence serves her well even when her knowledge itself attracts suspicion.
book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Jamie Fraser: A young Highlander living with the consequences of an encounter with the British army. His wit and tact are as important to Claire as his strength.
book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Frank Randall: Claire's twentieth-century husband is a historian absorbed in tracing his ancestry. Their second honeymoon is an attempt to recover intimacy after wartime separation.
book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Jonathan Randall: A British officer known as Black Jack Randall whose resemblance to Frank initially disorients Claire. Military authority gives his private sadism a wide reach.
book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Dougal MacKenzie: The MacKenzie war chief weighs Claire as a possible spy and a political asset. His charm seldom cancels out his calculation.
book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Colum MacKenzie: The clan leader governs through intellect, information and his brother's military strength. He receives an unknown guest with hospitality that doubles as an interrogation.
book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Geillis Duncan: A knowledgeable herbalist whose apparent familiarity with local belief makes her an intriguing friend and a dangerous person to be seen with.
book-diana-gabaldon-outlander.Murtagh Fitzgibbons Fraser: Jamie's godfather is a laconic Highlander with little interest in appearances. Once he gives his loyalty, practical help usually follows without a speech.

book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Frodo Baggins: Bilbo's heir is a hobbit with a taste for Elvish stories and an unusually strong sense of responsibility. Inheriting a ring gives that quality a terrible test.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Samwise Gamgee: Frodo's gardener loves growing things, listening to tales and making sure his master eats. His plain speech is capable of startling poetic feeling.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Gollum: Frodo's former pursuer offers his services as a guide. In conversations with himself, hope of being trusted keeps resurfacing against the possessive voice of the Ring.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Aragorn: A weatherbeaten Ranger called Strider keeps watch over people who scarcely know he protects them. He must earn the hobbits' trust without the privileges of rank.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Gandalf: A wandering wizard who engineers unlikely meetings and has great faith in a hobbit's usefulness. His advice often becomes clear only after he has left.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Legolas: An elven archer from the Woodland Realm hears and sees what his companions miss. Friendship on the road challenges an inherited suspicion of dwarves.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Gimli: Glóin's son represents his people with a warrior's pride and a craftsman's feeling for beautiful stone. Moria is family history for him.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Meriadoc Brandybuck: Frodo's practical cousin has thought ahead about the journey, the cover story and the baggage. His cheerfulness is backed by real preparations.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Peregrin Took: The youngest of the four hobbits brings curiosity, appetite and an imperfect sense of when to keep quiet. Courage is rarely his first impulse but often his second.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Treebeard: An Ent who thinks at the pace of a forest. His delight in meeting two hobbits slowly gives way to anger at what has happened to the trees.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Théoden: The aging king of Rohan must decide whom to trust after years of discouraging counsel. Returning to the saddle changes the way he inhabits his own hall.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Éomer: Théoden's nephew is a cavalry commander who takes risks at the border on his own judgment. Meeting Aragorn tests where loyal service permits disobedience.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Éowyn: A member of Rohan's royal household who cares for an aging uncle and longs for deeds of her own beyond the doors of the hall.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Gríma Wormtongue: Théoden's adviser has learned to present fear as caution. His power depends on discouraging the king from hearing any more hopeful voice.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Saruman: The head of the order of wizards has studied the Enemy closely. His persuasive voice can make accommodation with power sound like clear-sighted prudence.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Faramir: Boromir's younger brother commands rangers in Ithilien. Curiosity about a traveller's story gives him options a less thoughtful captain might miss.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Shelob: An ancient spider haunting the pass above Minas Morgul. Hunger, darkness and the geography of her tunnels make her a danger independent of anyone's politics.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Háma: The king's doorward judges which weapons and which visitors may enter. A small exercise of discretion has consequences for all of Rohan.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Erkenbrand: A lord of the Westfold whose scattered forces matter to the defence of Helm's Deep. His return in the book gives the defenders a new chance.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Quickbeam: A comparatively hasty Ent with a special affection for rowan trees. In his company even hobbits can feel what a damaged grove has lost.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Uglúk: The Uruk-hai captain responsible for delivering captured hobbits. He has to keep rival orcs moving together under pursuit and in daylight.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Shagrat: The captain at Cirith Ungol understands orders as a means of surviving his superiors. Meeting a rival patrol gives him someone with whom to compare grievances.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-two-towers.Gorbag: An orc commander from Minas Morgul whose conversation with Shagrat reveals the rivalries, resentments and private ambitions beneath Sauron's apparent unity.

book-ana-huang-twisted-games.Bridget von Ascheberg: A princess who would happily trade ceremony for a little privacy. A change in the succession puts her own choices under national scrutiny.
book-ana-huang-twisted-games.Rhys Larsen: A former military man assigned as Bridget's bodyguard. His clipped instructions conceal how closely he listens to what she wants for herself.
book-ana-huang-twisted-games.Nikolai von Ascheberg: Bridget's older brother must weigh personal happiness against his place in the succession. His decision has immediate consequences for his sister.
book-ana-huang-twisted-games.Prince Andreas: An ambitious royal relative who keeps close watch on Bridget's vulnerabilities. A private piece of information is more useful to him than a public insult.
book-ana-huang-twisted-games.King Edvard: Bridget's grandfather is both the monarch and a man worried about his family's future. He cannot treat her romantic choices as purely personal.

book-holly-black-the-wicked-king.Jude Duarte: A mortal raised among faeries, Jude trains with a sword and learns to exploit her ability to lie. She wants a real share of power at court.
book-holly-black-the-wicked-king.Cardan Greenbriar: A beautiful, frequently drunk faerie prince who makes a sport of humiliating Jude. His cruelty draws an audience and keeps that audience at a distance.
book-holly-black-the-wicked-king.Orlagh: The Queen of the Undersea speaks for a realm the land court cannot easily threaten. She treats her daughter's future as a matter of state.
book-holly-black-the-wicked-king.Nicasia: Orlagh's daughter grew up close to Cardan. Under her contempt for mortals lies the vulnerability of a princess whose mother expects a useful alliance.
book-holly-black-the-wicked-king.Madoc: A redcap general who raises the children of the parents he killed. He teaches Jude strategy with a father's pride and a conqueror's appetite.
book-holly-black-the-wicked-king.Balekin Greenbriar: Cardan's elder brother intends to rule. At home he treats punishment as a lesson and obedience as proof that the lesson worked.
book-holly-black-the-wicked-king.The Ghost: A soft-footed spy and archer in the Court of Shadows. He can teach Jude where to place a footstep without disclosing much about himself.

book-fyodor-dostoevsky-crime-and-punishm.Rodion Raskolnikov: An impoverished former student tests a theory that exceptional people may step outside ordinary morality. Fever and compulsive talk make him a poor keeper of his own counsel.
book-fyodor-dostoevsky-crime-and-punishm.Sofya Marmeladova: A young woman supporting her family through prostitution holds on to her faith. She can hear an appalling confession without reducing the speaker to the act.
book-fyodor-dostoevsky-crime-and-punishm.Porfiry Petrovich: The investigating magistrate prefers an apparently casual conversation to a direct accusation. He knows the discomfort of uncertainty can keep a suspect coming back.
book-fyodor-dostoevsky-crime-and-punishm.Avdotya Raskolnikova: Raskolnikov's sister weighs a financially advantageous marriage against its costs to her dignity. She is quite capable of judging the men who presume to protect her.
