book-fyodor-dostoevsky-crime-and-punishm.Dmitri Razumikhin: Raskolnikov's loyal friend has the energy to find food, work or a doctor when others can barely frame a question. His candour is as practical as his kindness.
book-fyodor-dostoevsky-crime-and-punishm.Arkady Svidrigailov: A wealthy former employer of Dunya combines generosity, predation and unnerving self-knowledge. His suggestions are especially disturbing when they echo Raskolnikov's private reasoning.

book-l-m-montgomery-anne-of-green-gables.Anne Shirley: An orphan with red hair and an enormous vocabulary arrives at a farm expecting a home. Giving places beautiful names is one way she makes herself belong.
book-l-m-montgomery-anne-of-green-gables.Marilla Cuthbert: A practical Prince Edward Island woman intends to correct an adoption mistake. Affection for Anne steadily complicates her ideas about discipline and duty.
book-l-m-montgomery-anne-of-green-gables.Matthew Cuthbert: Marilla's shy brother listens to Anne talk on the drive from the station. His quiet resolve occasionally proves firmer than his sister's much louder opinion.
book-l-m-montgomery-anne-of-green-gables.Diana Barry: The neighbour girl Anne claims as a bosom friend. Her dependable affection gives Anne someone with whom to test her grandest imaginative schemes.
book-l-m-montgomery-anne-of-green-gables.Gilbert Blythe: A clever schoolboy makes a disastrous first impression by teasing Anne about her hair. The long academic rivalry that follows is partly admiration in disguise.
book-l-m-montgomery-anne-of-green-gables.Rachel Lynde: An observant neighbour considers village affairs her legitimate business. Her blunt assessments can wound, but her practical loyalty is just as substantial.

book-liane-moriarty-big-little-lies.Madeline: An outspoken mother with a long memory for slights. She takes Jane under her wing and brings an entire school playground's politics along with her.
book-liane-moriarty-big-little-lies.Celeste: A former lawyer and mother of twins who appears to have an enviable marriage. She edits her accounts of ordinary evenings with extreme care.
book-liane-moriarty-big-little-lies.Jane: A young single mother hoping for a fresh start with her son. A schoolyard accusation threatens the quiet anonymity she came looking for.
book-liane-moriarty-big-little-lies.Perry: Celeste's charismatic husband is attentive in public. At home his changes of mood have taught her to anticipate danger long before anyone else sees it.
book-liane-moriarty-big-little-lies.Renata: A successful working mother who mobilizes quickly when her daughter reports being bullied. She expects a school to respond as decisively as she would.
book-liane-moriarty-big-little-lies.Bonnie: The younger wife of Madeline's ex-husband is calm in company and physically self-possessed. Madeline finds her generosity almost impossibly irritating.
book-liane-moriarty-big-little-lies.Ziggy: Jane's little boy arrives at a new school and is accused of hurting another child. His mother's need to understand competes with his need to be believed.

book-leigh-bardugo-shadow-and-bone.Alina Starkov: An orphan and army mapmaker whose power to summon light makes her suddenly indispensable. She is still learning what to do when a whole room looks at her.
book-leigh-bardugo-shadow-and-bone.Malyen Oretsev: Alina's childhood friend is an exceptionally gifted army tracker. In the field he notices the smallest change in the landscape, even when he misses one in her.
book-leigh-bardugo-shadow-and-bone.The Darkling: The shadow-summoning commander of Ravka's Grisha speaks about their persecution with intimate conviction. He knows exactly how it feels to be the only one of your kind.
book-leigh-bardugo-shadow-and-bone.Genya Safin: A Grisha Tailor who can alter a person's appearance. Serving the queen has taught her to offer kindness in a palace that treats beauty as currency.
book-leigh-bardugo-shadow-and-bone.Baghra: A formidable Grisha teacher who meets Alina's uncertainty with a stick and a cutting remark. She takes the consequences of power very seriously.
book-leigh-bardugo-shadow-and-bone.Zoya Nazyalensky: A gifted Squaller who commands the wind. She holds fellow Grisha to exacting standards and sees no reason to spare an unprepared newcomer her opinion.

book-lauren-roberts-powerless.Paedyn Gray: A powerless pickpocket who passes as psychic by reading people's smallest tells. Saving the wrong stranger puts her powers of observation on public trial.
book-lauren-roberts-powerless.Kai Azer: A prince trained to enforce his father's laws. He can borrow the powers of Elites nearby, but Paedyn's nerve interests him more than any display of magic.
book-lauren-roberts-powerless.Kitt Azer: Ilya's heir is accustomed to being the more approachable brother. Kindness comes easily until it puts him at odds with the crown he expects to wear.
book-lauren-roberts-powerless.Adena: Paedyn's closest friend sews beautiful clothes from scraps. She gives the two of them a sense of home in a city that leaves little room for either.
book-lauren-roberts-powerless.Blair Archer: A telekinetic competitor in the Purging Trials. She understands the advantages of attacking from a distance and letting a crowd see her power.

book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Alan Grant: A palaeontologist invited to evaluate Hammond's island. His knowledge of fossils becomes practical fieldcraft when he must guide two children among living dinosaurs.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Ellie Sattler: A palaeobotanist who notices what the park designers have planted as readily as what they have resurrected. Curiosity makes her a hands-on investigator.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Ian Malcolm: A mathematician who thinks the park's founders have mistaken modelling a system for controlling it. His wit makes the warning even more aggravating to them.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.John Hammond: The elderly promoter who finances the park sees an objection chiefly as a failure of imagination. His affection for his creation makes him dangerously hard to persuade.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Tim Murphy: Hammond's dinosaur-obsessed grandson can identify what the adults are seeing and find his way around a computer. His younger sister has different interests.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Lex Murphy: Tim's younger sister would rather talk baseball than dinosaurs. Her hunger, fear and impatience keep survival firmly at a child's scale.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Robert Muldoon: The park's game warden treats the animals as dangerous wildlife. His practical assessment has to compete with his employer's confidence in the attraction.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Dennis Nedry: The programmer responsible for critical park systems feels underpaid and unappreciated. He knows precisely how much inconvenience his absence can cause.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Henry Wu: The geneticist behind Hammond's dinosaurs wants credit for the technical achievement. He sees the animals as organisms his team can continue to redesign.
book-michael-crichton-jurassic-park.Donald Gennaro: A lawyer representing the park's financial interests arrives to assess liability. The inspection soon demands far more of him than a report to investors.

book-cormac-mccarthy-the-road.The Father: A dying father shepherds his son down a ruined road. Every abandoned house presents the same brutal calculation about shelter, food and strangers.
book-cormac-mccarthy-the-road.The Boy: A boy born after the catastrophe continually asks whether they can help the people they pass. His questions force his father to define goodness through action.
book-cormac-mccarthy-the-road.Ely: An elderly wanderer who offers a name the travellers cannot verify. The boy's wish to feed him opens a rare conversation about survival.
book-cormac-mccarthy-the-road.The Mother: The boy's mother appears in the father's memories. Her assessment of what the ruined world offers their child differs sharply from his determination to continue.

book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Frodo Baggins: Bilbo's heir is a hobbit with a taste for Elvish stories and an unusually strong sense of responsibility. Inheriting a ring gives that quality a terrible test.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Samwise Gamgee: With the Shire far behind, Sam thinks in terms of rations, routes and whether Frodo can take one more step. His gardener's eye still finds signs of life.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Aragorn: A weatherbeaten Ranger called Strider keeps watch over people who scarcely know he protects them. He must earn the hobbits' trust without the privileges of rank.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Gandalf: A wandering wizard who engineers unlikely meetings and has great faith in a hobbit's usefulness. His advice often becomes clear only after he has left.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Gollum: A solitary creature beneath the mountains who talks to himself and treasures a small ring. A game of riddles briefly gives him company as well as prey.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Peregrin Took: The youngest of the four hobbits brings curiosity, appetite and an imperfect sense of when to keep quiet. Courage is rarely his first impulse but often his second.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Meriadoc Brandybuck: Frodo's practical cousin has thought ahead about the journey, the cover story and the baggage. His cheerfulness is backed by real preparations.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Éowyn: A member of Rohan's royal household who cares for an aging uncle and longs for deeds of her own beyond the doors of the hall.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Faramir: Boromir's younger brother commands rangers in Ithilien. Curiosity about a traveller's story gives him options a less thoughtful captain might miss.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Denethor II: Gondor's steward has held his city against long odds and resents anyone who questions his judgment. His two sons experience his expectations very differently.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Théoden: The aging king of Rohan must decide whom to trust after years of discouraging counsel. Returning to the saddle changes the way he inhabits his own hall.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Éomer: Théoden's nephew is a cavalry commander who takes risks at the border on his own judgment. Meeting Aragorn tests where loyal service permits disobedience.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Legolas: An elven archer from the Woodland Realm hears and sees what his companions miss. Friendship on the road challenges an inherited suspicion of dwarves.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Gimli: Glóin's son represents his people with a warrior's pride and a craftsman's feeling for beautiful stone. Moria is family history for him.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.The Witch-king of Angmar: The chief of the Ringwraiths pursues the Ring-bearer with terrifying persistence. Riders, weather and the courage of his opponents change in his presence.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Sauron: The power ruling Mordor searches for his lost Ring. His presence is felt chiefly through scrutiny, commands and the fear of attracting his full attention.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Imrahil: The Prince of Dol Amroth brings experienced troops to Minas Tirith. Courtesy and keen observation make him a valuable ally amid the confusion of battle.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Beregond: A soldier of Gondor who welcomes Pippin and takes his oath seriously. Loyalty to a person can place him in painful conflict with an order.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Arwen: Elrond's daughter is glimpsed at Rivendell through a hobbit's eyes. Her quiet connection to Aragorn hints at the private stakes of his long service.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Halbarad: A northern Ranger who brings Aragorn reinforcements and a furled standard. Their long comradeship gives weight to his willingness to follow a perilous route.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Ghan-buri-Ghan: The leader of the Drúedain knows paths an invading army has overlooked. He offers guidance while asking that his own people finally be left in peace.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.The Mouth of Sauron: Sauron's emissary uses language and carefully chosen objects to frighten an army at the Black Gate. He expects negotiation to amount to submission.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Ioreth: A woman working in the Houses of Healing whose stock of old sayings contains a clue of real practical importance. Once started, she enjoys a good conversation.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Saruman: The head of the order of wizards has studied the Enemy closely. His persuasive voice can make accommodation with power sound like clear-sighted prudence.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Gríma Wormtongue: Théoden's adviser has learned to present fear as caution. His power depends on discouraging the king from hearing any more hopeful voice.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Rosie Cotton: A farmer's daughter in the Shire with a long-standing affection for Sam. Her frank welcome puts the travellers' grand adventures in a homely perspective.
book-j-r-r-tolkien-the-return-of-the-kin.Farmer Cotton: Rosie's father is well informed about what has happened in the Shire. Local knowledge and neighbours willing to act make him invaluable to the returning hobbits.

book-taylor-jenkins-reid-atmosphere.Joan Goodwin: A physics and astronomy professor entering NASA's astronaut programme. Her quiet delight in the stars sits alongside the discipline to talk someone through an emergency.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-atmosphere.Vanessa Ford: An aeronautical engineer and gifted pilot. In training, Joan sees both Vanessa's relish for a difficult mechanical problem and the privacy she guards off duty.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-atmosphere.Frances Goodwin: Joan's young niece asks direct questions and expects her aunt to take them seriously. Their shared delight in space gives the programme a child's-eye scale.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-atmosphere.Donna Fitzgerald: A warm fellow astronaut candidate who understands the stakes of being judged in public. She builds friendships while keeping parts of her own life private.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-atmosphere.John Griffin: A scientist training alongside Joan. He brings an easygoing manner into demanding exercises where colleagues need to trust the person beside them.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-atmosphere.Hank Redman: A highly skilled military pilot entering astronaut training. His relaxed manner lets the other candidates glimpse the person behind the competitive résumé.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-atmosphere.Barbara Goodwin: Joan's sister and Frances's mother. She expects substantial help with her daughter, leaving Joan to negotiate where being an aunt ends and parenting begins.

book-alexandre-dumas-the-count-of-monte-.Edmond Dantès: A young Marseille sailor with a promotion and marriage in prospect is imprisoned on a false accusation. The patience he develops in captivity later takes unsettling forms.
book-alexandre-dumas-the-count-of-monte-.Mercédès: Edmond's Catalan fiancée builds a life around a disappearance nobody can explain. Recognition asks more of her than anyone around her realizes.
book-alexandre-dumas-the-count-of-monte-.Fernand Mondego: A rival for Mercédès's affections carries an early act of jealousy into an illustrious military career. The more he rises, the more he needs the past kept buried.
book-alexandre-dumas-the-count-of-monte-.Gérard de Villefort: An ambitious prosecutor knows the difference between evidence and political danger. In Edmond's case he chooses his career, with consequences that reach his own family.
book-alexandre-dumas-the-count-of-monte-.Baron Danglars: An envious ship's accountant turns financial calculation into a career. Wealth alters his public standing far more than it alters his vulnerabilities.
book-alexandre-dumas-the-count-of-monte-.Abbé Faria: An imprisoned priest tunnels into Edmond's life and becomes his teacher. Their friendship gives the younger man both an education and an altered sense of possibility.
book-alexandre-dumas-the-count-of-monte-.Haydée: The daughter of Ali Pasha lives under the Count's protection. Memories others treat as political history are, for her, the destruction of her family.

book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Tyrion Lannister: A wealthy lord's son with dwarfism has learned to enter a room anticipating the joke. Books, money and a precise insult are among his defences.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Arya Stark: A lord's daughter who would rather learn swordplay than needlework. She pays more attention to servants, animals and escapes than her elders realize.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Jon Snow: Raised as Ned Stark's bastard, Jon knows the household intimately while remaining conscious of his place at its edge. The Night's Watch offers a different brotherhood.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Sansa Stark: Arya's older sister loves songs of gallant knights and knows how a lady should behave. At court, courtesy acquires uses her songs never taught her.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Theon Greyjoy: Balon Greyjoy's son grew up as Ned Stark's ward and hostage. Returning to the Iron Islands means finding out whether his own family considers him one of them.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Davos Seaworth: A former smuggler raised to knighthood by Stannis. Gratitude makes him loyal enough to give his king advice nobody more polished dares to offer.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Catelyn Stark: Lady of Winterfell, born a Tully, she reads politics through kinship, promises and danger to her children. Urgency can make her act before her allies are ready.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Bran Stark: A boy who loves climbing the walls of Winterfell and imagining himself a knight. His connection to his direwolf grows harder to explain.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Daenerys Targaryen: An exiled Targaryen girl traded into marriage by her brother. Learning another language and another people's customs gives her room to discover authority of her own.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Stannis Baratheon: Robert's brother believes the succession is a matter of law. He remembers debts and slights with extraordinary precision and finds being liked a poor substitute for being right.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Melisandre: A priestess of the Lord of Light who interprets visions in flame. Her certainty offers Stannis a kind of recognition his countrymen have withheld.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Renly Baratheon: Robert's youngest brother has charm, a glittering court and a considerable army. His claim asks whether popularity can make a king.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Brienne of Tarth: A physically powerful swordswoman mocked for wanting to live by a knight's vows. An act of courtesy from Renly has earned him her devotion.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Cersei Lannister: The queen guards her children and her position with equal ferocity. A lifetime of watching her twin receive freedoms denied to her feeds her political ambition.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Joffrey Baratheon: The crown prince has been told all his life that deference is his due. He is especially dangerous when an audience witnesses an embarrassment.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Ygritte: A free woman from beyond the Wall who finds Jon's assumptions about wildlings as strange as he finds hers. Teasing gives her lessons a memorable edge.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Tywin Lannister: The Lannister patriarch understands armies, money and the calculated public insult. He expects his children to serve a family name he alone gets to define.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-clash-of-kings.Robb Stark: The eldest Stark son has learned to command beside his father. When adults look to him for decisions, the distance between boy and lord shrinks abruptly.

book-mark-twain-the-adventures-of-tom-sa.Tom Sawyer: Tom can make fence painting look like a privilege and a cave look like a kingdom. Real danger asks more of him than the games he invents.
book-mark-twain-the-adventures-of-tom-sa.Huckleberry Finn: Tom's friend lives outside the routines of school, church and Sunday clothes. The boys who envy that freedom seldom notice how little protection comes with it.
book-mark-twain-the-adventures-of-tom-sa.Becky Thatcher: Tom's new classmate shares his taste for attentions and quarrels. A schoolgirl courtship asks more courage of both when they wander into a cave.
book-mark-twain-the-adventures-of-tom-sa.Aunt Polly: Tom's aunt tries discipline, home remedies and appeals to conscience. The boy knows her weaknesses because her affection for him is genuine.
book-mark-twain-the-adventures-of-tom-sa.Injun Joe: A man with an old grievance whose violence Tom witnesses. His presence turns familiar spots around town into places where a child's testimony could be dangerous.
book-mark-twain-the-adventures-of-tom-sa.Muff Potter: A poor townsman vulnerable to drink and accusation. The kindness he has shown the boys makes keeping silent about what they saw particularly hard.

book-charles-dickens-a-tale-of-two-citie.Sydney Carton: A gifted legal assistant lets another man take public credit for much of his intelligence. Lucie's regard interrupts his conviction that his life is wasted.
book-charles-dickens-a-tale-of-two-citie.Charles Darnay: A French émigré trying to earn his own living in England. Renouncing his family's conduct does little to prevent others from holding him responsible for its name.
book-charles-dickens-a-tale-of-two-citie.Lucie Manette: Doctor Manette's daughter builds a home around a father she scarcely remembers. Her steadiness becomes a point of reference for men with sharply divided lives.
book-charles-dickens-a-tale-of-two-citie.Alexandre Manette: A physician returns from years of imprisonment in the Bastille. His daughter's presence restores much, although the habits of his cell remain within reach.
book-charles-dickens-a-tale-of-two-citie.Madame Defarge: A Paris wine-shop keeper records names in her knitting. Private injury and political vengeance have become nearly inseparable in her idea of justice.
book-charles-dickens-a-tale-of-two-citie.Jarvis Lorry: A banker who introduces himself as a man of business while repeatedly extending the Manettes a loyalty that no bank requires.

book-john-steinbeck-the-grapes-of-wrath.Tom Joad: A recently paroled Oklahoman comes home to find his family displaced. His instinct to look after his own broadens on the road west.
book-john-steinbeck-the-grapes-of-wrath.Ma Joad: The Joad matriarch feeds, counts and keeps track of everybody. As familiar structures collapse, the family increasingly relies on decisions she makes without ceremony.
book-john-steinbeck-the-grapes-of-wrath.Jim Casy: A former preacher questions the difference between individual holiness and collective responsibility. Fellow workers become the congregation for his changing beliefs.
book-john-steinbeck-the-grapes-of-wrath.Rose of Sharon Joad: A pregnant young woman dreams of a settled household in California. The road keeps separating the future she imagined from the needs in front of her.
book-john-steinbeck-the-grapes-of-wrath.Pa Joad: The family's dispossessed father sets out expecting to find work and resume his accustomed role. Authority shifts as that hope becomes harder to sustain.
book-john-steinbeck-the-grapes-of-wrath.Al Joad: Tom's younger brother understands engines and would like credit for being grown. Keeping the family's vehicle running gives that desire a concrete responsibility.

book-holly-black-the-queen-of-nothing.Jude Duarte: A mortal raised among faeries, Jude trains with a sword and learns to exploit her ability to lie. She wants a real share of power at court.
book-holly-black-the-queen-of-nothing.Cardan Greenbriar: A beautiful, frequently drunk faerie prince who makes a sport of humiliating Jude. His cruelty draws an audience and keeps that audience at a distance.
book-holly-black-the-queen-of-nothing.Madoc: A redcap general who raises the children of the parents he killed. He teaches Jude strategy with a father's pride and a conqueror's appetite.
book-holly-black-the-queen-of-nothing.Taryn Duarte: Jude's twin thinks a mortal can secure a place in Faerie by learning its rules. The bargains she accepts test the closeness of the sisters.
book-holly-black-the-queen-of-nothing.Grima Mog: A formidable redcap commander living among humans. Her blunt assessment of a fighter carries more weight than any courtly introduction.
book-holly-black-the-queen-of-nothing.The Ghost: A soft-footed spy and archer in the Court of Shadows. He can teach Jude where to place a footstep without disclosing much about himself.
book-holly-black-the-queen-of-nothing.Grimsen: A faerie smith whose creations can change the balance of power. He is exquisitely sensitive to the respect he believes an artist is owed.

book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Bryce Quinlan: A half-Fae gallery employee with a dancer's feet and a party girl's reputation. Jokes come easily, especially when somebody gets close to her grief.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Hunt Athalar: An enslaved angel and highly trained killer. Away from orders and surveillance, he would happily spend an afternoon watching sunball on the couch.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Ruhn Danaan: A Fae crown prince with a lip ring, a chosen family of friends and a prickly tenderness for his half-sister Bryce.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Rigelus: One of the Asteri who rule Midgard, Rigelus speaks with centuries of authority from a body that looks disconcertingly young.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Cormac Donnall: An Avallen prince whose proposed marriage to Bryce serves their fathers' politics. His severity makes it difficult to tell what he wants for himself.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Tharion Ketos: A mer captain who investigates for the River Queen. Easy flirtation on dry land gives him a taste of freedom his position rarely affords him.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Ithan Holstrom: A young wolf shifter and former sunball player. Loyalty to his brother and pack weighs heavily on a man used to thinking as a teammate.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-sky-and-breat.Lidia Cervos: Known as the Hind, this deer shifter has earned a terrifying reputation in the Asteri's service. People choose their words very carefully around her.

book-jane-austen-emma.Emma Woodhouse: A wealthy young woman with enough leisure to arrange other people's love lives. Her imagination can build an entire courtship from a single agreeable conversation.
book-jane-austen-emma.George Knightley: Emma's longtime neighbour combines easy familiarity with an inconvenient willingness to disagree. He pays attention to the people her matchmaking plans tend to overlook.
book-jane-austen-emma.Harriet Smith: A warm, impressionable schoolgirl uncertain of her parentage. Being noticed by Emma expands her hopes and makes her distrust some perfectly sensible instincts.
book-jane-austen-emma.Frank Churchill: A charming visitor whose playful hints keep Highbury absorbed. His dependence on an exacting aunt gives him reasons to manage what people believe.
book-jane-austen-emma.Jane Fairfax: An accomplished young woman facing the prospect of earning her living as a governess. Reserve protects her privacy while encouraging Emma to invent explanations.
book-jane-austen-emma.Philip Elton: Highbury's ambitious clergyman accepts invitations and compliments with enthusiasm. Emma's interpretation of the woman he hopes to marry misses a crucial distinction of rank.

book-abby-jimenez-part-of-your-world.Alexis Montgomery: An emergency physician from a prominent medical family. In Daniel's small town she can spend an evening as herself without carrying her family's name into the room.
book-abby-jimenez-part-of-your-world.Daniel Grant: A younger carpenter and small-town mayor with deep roots in his community. His hospitality includes making things with his hands and showing up when needed.
book-abby-jimenez-part-of-your-world.Briana Ortiz: Alexis's close friend and fellow emergency physician. She hears the hesitation behind Alexis's polished explanations and is willing to say so.
book-abby-jimenez-part-of-your-world.Neil Rasmussen: Alexis's former partner is a respected surgeon who expects their separation to be temporary. Professional prestige helps camouflage his controlling behaviour.

book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-played-w.Lisbeth Salander: A freelance investigator and gifted hacker who remembers insults and details with equal precision. She guards her autonomy fiercely after years of official interference.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-played-w.Mikael Blomkvist: A journalist facing a professional disgrace accepts a wealthy industrialist's old family mystery. He gets people talking by actually listening to them.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-played-w.Paolo Roberto: A professional boxer who knows Lisbeth through training. When someone connected to her needs help, he takes a much more direct route than a journalist might.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-played-w.Alexander Zalachenko: A former Soviet intelligence operative with a clandestine history in Sweden. Institutions that once found him useful have reasons to keep that history quiet.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-played-w.Ronald Niedermann: An enforcer whose massive strength is matched by an unusual inability to feel pain. His eerie composure changes the terms of a physical confrontation.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-played-w.Miriam Wu: Lisbeth's friend and occasional lover values her independence. Public fascination with their relationship puts her in danger without giving her a say.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-played-w.Sonja Modig: A police investigator willing to examine whether the emerging public story about Lisbeth fits the evidence her colleagues actually possess.

book-stephanie-garber-caraval.Scarlett Dragna: A protective older sister who has spent years writing to Caraval's mysterious master. Once inside the game, she has difficulty trusting even her own senses.
book-stephanie-garber-caraval.Donatella Dragna: Scarlett's adventurous younger sister is considerably more willing to gamble on a stranger or a magical invitation if it offers a way out of home.
book-stephanie-garber-caraval.Julian Santos: A sailor with a teasing manner and an inconvenient habit of knowing more about Caraval than he will tell Scarlett.
book-stephanie-garber-caraval.Legend: Caraval's master builds an entire performance around the question of who he really is. His most effective instrument is often the audience's imagination.
book-stephanie-garber-caraval.Marcello Dragna: The governor and the Dragna sisters' father. He keeps his daughters obedient by making each feel responsible for what happens to the other.

book-abby-jimenez-yours-truly.Briana Ortiz: An ER doctor moving through a divorce and her brother's illness is convinced she has sized up a new colleague. A handwritten letter changes the conversation.
book-abby-jimenez-yours-truly.Jacob Maddox: A new emergency physician with social anxiety. Writing letters lets him show Briana the funny, thoughtful man she missed during their disastrous first meeting.
book-abby-jimenez-yours-truly.Benny Ortiz: Briana's younger brother is waiting for a kidney transplant. Being loved by a fiercely protective sister doesn't erase the exhausting uncertainty of the wait.
book-abby-jimenez-yours-truly.Alexis Montgomery: An emergency physician from a prominent medical family. In Daniel's small town she can spend an evening as herself without carrying her family's name into the room.

book-leo-tolstoy-anna-karenina.Anna Karenina: A married woman accustomed to reading a drawing room accurately. Passion for Vronsky exposes the cruelty of a society whose manners she once navigated with ease.
book-leo-tolstoy-anna-karenina.Konstantin Levin: A landowner finds mowing alongside labourers easier than making conversation in a salon. Love, work and questions of faith occupy him with equal intensity.
book-leo-tolstoy-anna-karenina.Alexei Vronsky: A cavalry officer used to moving easily between regimental and aristocratic company. His attraction to Anna puts that ease at odds with public judgment.
book-leo-tolstoy-anna-karenina.Alexei Karenin: Anna's husband is a government official skilled in managing appearances. Private humiliation forces him into emotional territory for which official language serves him poorly.
book-leo-tolstoy-anna-karenina.Kitty Shcherbatskaya: A young woman whose romantic disappointment unsettles the adult life she had imagined. Nursing and marriage bring out capacities she scarcely knew she had.
book-leo-tolstoy-anna-karenina.Stiva Oblonsky: Anna's genial brother expects affection and forgiveness to survive his infidelities. His genuine warmth makes the cost others bear for him easy to overlook.
book-leo-tolstoy-anna-karenina.Dolly Oblonskaya: Stiva's wife manages a large family while enduring her husband's betrayals. Financial detail and the needs of children shape her view of romantic freedom.

book-charles-dickens-a-christmas-carol.Ebenezer Scrooge: A moneylender who regards Christmas as an expensive interruption. Revisiting his own boyhood exposes feelings he has spent decades treating as bad accounting.
book-charles-dickens-a-christmas-carol.Bob Cratchit: Scrooge's underpaid clerk finds reasons to celebrate at a crowded family table. Cheerfulness requires effort when a child's health depends on a tiny wage.
book-charles-dickens-a-christmas-carol.Jacob Marley: Scrooge's dead business partner returns carrying a chain of ledgers, keys and cashboxes. He has one night to make an old colleague listen.
book-charles-dickens-a-christmas-carol.Tiny Tim: The Cratchits' young son goes to church with his father and insists on raising his voice in the family toast. His siblings know just how to make room for him.
book-charles-dickens-a-christmas-carol.Ghost of Christmas Past: A spirit who escorts Scrooge through scenes he knows intimately and would much rather forget. Its light offers illumination he cannot always stand.
book-charles-dickens-a-christmas-carol.Ghost of Christmas Present: A great laughing figure who takes Scrooge into homes he ordinarily ignores. Hospitality and rebuke come equally naturally to this short-lived guide.
book-charles-dickens-a-christmas-carol.Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come: A hooded figure lets Scrooge overhear the future without answering his questions. A pointed hand does nearly all the communicating.

book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Buttercup: A farm girl celebrated for her beauty discovers that ordering the farm boy about has become a kind of courtship. She has a stubborn streak to match his.
book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Westley: A farm boy with extravagant faith in Buttercup and an astonishing capacity for learning new skills. Even a duel can become a courteous conversation.
book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Inigo Montoya: A Spanish swordsman has rehearsed a single introduction for most of his life. Craftsmanship, courtesy and grief give his quest its peculiar dignity.
book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Fezzik: A giant who loves rhymes and worries about being left alone. His gentleness is especially striking when everyone hires him for his strength.
book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Prince Humperdinck: A prince who measures nearly everything by its usefulness in a hunt. Even arranging a marriage fits smoothly into his political calculations.
book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Count Rugen: The six-fingered count approaches cruelty as an opportunity for research. His interest in taking precise measurements makes him a particularly chilling host.
book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Vizzini: A self-proclaimed genius who hires exceptional men and reminds them which one is in charge. He confuses verbal superiority with having anticipated every move.
book-william-goldman-the-princess-bride.Miracle Max: A former royal miracle worker receives an unusual request in retirement. Old professional pride can still be stirred with the right inducement.

book-nathaniel-hawthorne-the-scarlet-let.Hester Prynne: A woman publicly marked for adultery supports herself and her daughter by needlework. Her composure gives townspeople ample room to misread her convictions.
book-nathaniel-hawthorne-the-scarlet-let.Arthur Dimmesdale: A Puritan minister is esteemed for preaching that grows more moving as his private anguish deepens. Public admiration makes confession harder.
book-nathaniel-hawthorne-the-scarlet-let.Roger Chillingworth: Hester's estranged husband arrives as a learned physician. Professional access to another man's suffering gradually becomes a means of pursuing revenge.
book-nathaniel-hawthorne-the-scarlet-let.Pearl: Hester's daughter is imaginative, perceptive and fascinated by the scarlet letter. Her direct questions expose arrangements the adults have learned to leave unspoken.

A carer recalling her English boarding-school years notices tiny shifts in a friendship. Her composed voice rarely announces the full weight of a memory.
A Hailsham pupil whose sudden rages make him a target for teasing. With Kathy he can voice the questions adults have left unanswered.
book-kazuo-ishiguro-never-let-me-go.Ruth: A charismatic schoolfriend who invents insider knowledge to keep a group around her. Her need for closeness often takes the form of controlling it.
book-kazuo-ishiguro-never-let-me-go.Miss Lucy: A Hailsham guardian troubled by what the students have been allowed to assume. She struggles to stay within the school's careful vocabulary.
book-kazuo-ishiguro-never-let-me-go.Miss Emily: Hailsham's head guardian has a formidable presence and a precise idea of the school's purpose. She decides which truths children are ready to hear.
book-kazuo-ishiguro-never-let-me-go.Madame: A visitor who selects pupils' artwork for a mysterious gallery. Her visible unease around the children makes them curious about their place in the world.

book-barbara-kingsolver-demon-copperhead.Damon Fields: A red-haired Appalachian boy with a quick tongue and a gift for drawing. Telling his own story lets him answer institutions that have spoken for him.
book-barbara-kingsolver-demon-copperhead.Angus Winfield: The coach's daughter is used to people making the wrong assumption from her nickname. She gives Demon a friendship grounded in unsentimental honesty.
book-barbara-kingsolver-demon-copperhead.Dori: A young woman caring for an ill father when Demon meets her. The tenderness between them becomes entangled with dependency and access to painkillers.
book-barbara-kingsolver-demon-copperhead.Fast Forward: An older foster boy and charismatic athlete who knows how to acquire followers. His favour feels especially valuable to boys with no reliable protection.
book-barbara-kingsolver-demon-copperhead.Maggot: Demon's childhood friend grows up next door in the Peggot household. Their shared private world outlasts many of the adults' arrangements for them.
book-barbara-kingsolver-demon-copperhead.Coach Winfield: A local football coach gives Demon a home and a place on the team. His genuine investment in the boy comes with the town's enormous expectations.
book-barbara-kingsolver-demon-copperhead.Miss Betsy Woodall: Demon's paternal grandmother has a formidable presence and clear ideas about helping children. Reaching her front door takes extraordinary resolve.

book-emily-henry-great-big-beautiful-lif.Alice Scott: A magazine writer with a gift for getting strangers to talk. A chance to tell Margaret Ives's story puts her optimism to a professional test.
book-emily-henry-great-big-beautiful-lif.Hayden Anderson: A decorated biographer competing with Alice for the same assignment. He measures his words as carefully as he examines a source's account.
book-emily-henry-great-big-beautiful-lif.Margaret Ives: An aging heiress who grew up in the headlines. She invites two writers to hear her story and retains precise control over what each gets to hear.
book-emily-henry-great-big-beautiful-lif.Cosmo Sinclair: A young rock-and-roll star whose connection to Margaret becomes tabloid property. Behind the famous name is a boy learning what celebrity costs.

book-jennifer-l-armentrout-from-blood-an.Penellaphe Balfour (Poppy): A veiled Maiden raised for a sacred role that leaves little room for choice. Secret weapons training is one of the few things she does for herself.
book-jennifer-l-armentrout-from-blood-an.Casteel Da’Neer (Hawke): A new guard called Hawke whose irreverence startles Poppy. He treats her curiosity as something to encourage, a startling departure from palace custom.
book-jennifer-l-armentrout-from-blood-an.Vikter Wardwell: Poppy's guard and trusted teacher has quietly taught her to defend herself. Protecting her sometimes means defying the household charged with her safety.
book-jennifer-l-armentrout-from-blood-an.Tawny Lyon: Poppy's companion shares confidences and eases the isolation imposed on the Maiden. She knows the person who lives behind the ceremonial veil.
book-jennifer-l-armentrout-from-blood-an.Dorian Teerman: The Duke of Masadonia exercises authority over Poppy's upbringing. His language of duty gives him cover for punishments he enjoys imposing.
book-jennifer-l-armentrout-from-blood-an.Kieran Contou: A dryly observant wolven warrior close to Hawke. He answers Poppy's endless questions with a mixture of patience, candour and amusement.

book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.The bank robber: A desperate parent attempts a bank robbery for painfully ordinary reasons. Apologizing to the people at an apartment viewing proves easier than controlling them.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Jack: A young police officer intent on untangling contradictory witness statements. His impatience is sharpened by having his father as a partner.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Jim: Jack's father is an experienced officer more inclined to let somebody finish a story. He and his son carry the same loss in different ways.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Zara: A wealthy bank director visits apartment viewings alone. Her caustic replies defend a private preoccupation with the view outside the windows.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Anna-Lena: Roger's wife has developed quiet strategies for keeping him occupied and their marriage companionable. She sees the people behind a negotiation.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Roger: A retired man who treats property viewings like competitive sport. Measuring a room gives him something definite to do when conversation becomes uncertain.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Julia: A heavily pregnant prospective buyer with direct opinions about apartments. Impending parenthood has made her especially impatient with indecision.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Ro: Julia's partner worries about finding the right home and becoming a good parent. Wit is a useful defence against both anxieties.
book-fredrik-backman-anxious-people.Estelle: An elderly woman at the viewing seems delighted to have company. Her hospitality makes more sense as the others discover her connection to the place.

book-charles-dickens-great-expectations.Pip: A blacksmith's apprentice comes into money and begins to imagine a gentleman's future. His embarrassment about his origins hurts because he loves the people he grew up with.
book-charles-dickens-great-expectations.Estella Havisham: Miss Havisham's ward has been taught to attract devotion without returning it. Her frank warnings to Pip are among the kindest things she offers him.
book-charles-dickens-great-expectations.Abel Magwitch: An escaped convict terrifies a small boy into helping him. Beneath the frightening manner lies an enduring memory of hunger, class injustice and unexpected kindness.
book-charles-dickens-great-expectations.Miss Havisham: A wealthy recluse keeps her bridal clothes and wedding feast long after the intended day. She invites children into a drama whose injury is entirely adult.
book-charles-dickens-great-expectations.Joe Gargery: Pip's brother-in-law is a skilled blacksmith who feels clumsy in grand company. He handles a frightened or embarrassed boy with extraordinary delicacy.
book-charles-dickens-great-expectations.Herbert Pocket: A cheerful young gentleman teaches Pip London table manners without making him feel small. His friendship has more substance than his business prospects.
book-charles-dickens-great-expectations.Jaggers: An intimidating lawyer who keeps his professional knowledge strictly compartmentalized. Precise questions and a conspicuous habit of washing his hands define his working day.

book-stephen-king-carrie.Carrie White: A bullied teenager raised in religious terror discovers she can move things with her mind. An invitation to prom briefly makes ordinary happiness seem possible.
book-stephen-king-carrie.Sue Snell: A popular student troubled by her part in humiliating Carrie. She tries to make amends by arranging an evening somebody else must actually live through.
book-stephen-king-carrie.Margaret White: Carrie's mother treats puberty and independence as evidence of sin. Her terror for her daughter's soul becomes a source of terror in their home.
book-stephen-king-carrie.Chris Hargensen: A high-school bully who regards punishment as an insult to her standing. She has the confidence and the resources to enlist others in her revenge.
book-stephen-king-carrie.Tommy Ross: Sue's boyfriend agrees to take Carrie to the prom. His willingness to be kind in public matters more to Carrie than he could know.
book-stephen-king-carrie.Billy Nolan: Chris's boyfriend brings a more dangerous appetite for cruelty to her scheme. He is considerably less amenable to being directed than she imagines.
book-stephen-king-carrie.Rita Desjardin: The gym teacher recognizes Carrie's distress and disciplines her tormentors. Her impulse to protect a vulnerable student sets her against some powerful parents.

book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Bryce Quinlan: A half-Fae gallery employee with a dancer's feet and a party girl's reputation. Jokes come easily, especially when somebody gets close to her grief.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Hunt Athalar: An enslaved angel and highly trained killer. Away from orders and surveillance, he would happily spend an afternoon watching sunball on the couch.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Ruhn Danaan: A Fae crown prince with a lip ring, a chosen family of friends and a prickly tenderness for his half-sister Bryce.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Lidia Cervos: Known as the Hind, this deer shifter has earned a terrifying reputation in the Asteri's service. People choose their words very carefully around her.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Ithan Holstrom: A young wolf shifter and former sunball player. Loyalty to his brother and pack weighs heavily on a man used to thinking as a teammate.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Tharion Ketos: A mer captain who investigates for the River Queen. Easy flirtation on dry land gives him a taste of freedom his position rarely affords him.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Nesta Archeron: A sharp-tongued Fae warrior from another world. Faced with a stranger on unfamiliar ground, she is slow to offer trust and quick to draw a blade.
book-sarah-j-maas-house-of-flame-and-sha.Rigelus: One of the Asteri who rule Midgard, Rigelus speaks with centuries of authority from a body that looks disconcertingly young.

book-ana-huang-twisted-hate.Jules Ambrose: A sharp-tongued aspiring lawyer who enjoys verbal combat with Josh. She has worked hard to build a future her past could still put in jeopardy.
book-ana-huang-twisted-hate.Josh Chen: A young doctor who enjoys trading insults with his sister's best friend. Private attraction complicates a rivalry he had always thought was safely mutual.
book-ana-huang-twisted-hate.Max: Jules's former boyfriend knows things about her earlier life that she has kept from the people closest to her. He intends to make that knowledge pay.
book-ana-huang-twisted-hate.Ava Chen: A photography student who looks for beauty as a matter of habit. Recurring gaps in her childhood memories complicate her apparent openness.

book-christina-lauren-love-and-other-wor.Macy Sorensen: A physician settled into a sensible engagement. Seeing her childhood best friend again brings back the frank, bookish girl she used to be with him.
book-christina-lauren-love-and-other-wor.Elliot Petropoulos: Macy's boyhood neighbour grew up trading favourite words with her in a makeshift library. As an adult he still asks questions that demand an honest answer.
book-christina-lauren-love-and-other-wor.Sean: Macy's fiancé is an older man with a daughter. Their orderly life together makes few demands on the parts of her past she keeps private.
book-christina-lauren-love-and-other-wor.Duncan Sorensen: Macy's widowed father buys a weekend house where his daughter can take a breath. Practical acts of care carry much of the feeling between them.

book-richard-osman-the-thursday-murder-c.Elizabeth Best: A retired woman with an unusually useful network of old contacts. She directs an amateur murder investigation with the precision of someone who has done this before.
book-richard-osman-the-thursday-murder-c.Joyce Meadowcroft: A former nurse and new club member whose chatty observations catch people off guard. Her diary records clues alongside the everyday pleasures of retirement.
book-richard-osman-the-thursday-murder-c.Ibrahim Arif: A retired psychiatrist with an exact mind and an appreciation for risk calculations. He supplies the club with structure when its theories multiply.
book-richard-osman-the-thursday-murder-c.Ron Ritchie: A former union organizer never entirely off duty. He is prepared to pick a very public fight if it helps a friend get answers.
book-richard-osman-the-thursday-murder-c.Donna De Freitas: An ambitious young police officer who would like a proper investigation. Four retirees turn out to be a very effective, if unofficial, route into one.
book-richard-osman-the-thursday-murder-c.Chris Hudson: A senior detective balancing police procedure with the club's remarkable access to gossip. His solitary habits leave room for some unexpected friendships.

book-gillian-flynn-dark-places.Libby Day: The survivor of a family massacre has lived for years on other people's sympathy. A paying invitation to revisit the case tests her own childhood testimony.
book-gillian-flynn-dark-places.Ben Day: Libby's imprisoned brother was a withdrawn teenager when the family died. Other people have long supplied explanations for things he refuses to discuss.
book-gillian-flynn-dark-places.Patty Day: A single mother struggling to keep a Kansas farm and four children afloat. Even a small bill can narrow her choices frighteningly.
book-gillian-flynn-dark-places.Lyle Wirth: An enthusiast for unsolved crimes who approaches Libby on behalf of a club. His interest in evidence feels uncomfortably different from hers.
book-gillian-flynn-dark-places.Diondra Wertzner: A volatile, privileged girl involved with teenage Ben. Their relationship belongs to a part of his life the rest of the Day family never saw.

book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Jaime Lannister: A gifted knight known chiefly for killing the king he swore to guard. His insolence makes an effective shield against other people's certainty about his motives.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Brienne of Tarth: A physically powerful swordswoman mocked for wanting to live by a knight's vows. An act of courtesy from Renly has earned him her devotion.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Tyrion Lannister: A wealthy lord's son with dwarfism has learned to enter a room anticipating the joke. Books, money and a precise insult are among his defences.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Catelyn Stark: Lady of Winterfell, born a Tully, she reads politics through kinship, promises and danger to her children. Urgency can make her act before her allies are ready.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Arya Stark: A lord's daughter who would rather learn swordplay than needlework. She pays more attention to servants, animals and escapes than her elders realize.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Sansa Stark: Arya's older sister loves songs of gallant knights and knows how a lady should behave. At court, courtesy acquires uses her songs never taught her.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Jon Snow: Raised as Ned Stark's bastard, Jon knows the household intimately while remaining conscious of his place at its edge. The Night's Watch offers a different brotherhood.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Daenerys Targaryen: An exiled Targaryen girl traded into marriage by her brother. Learning another language and another people's customs gives her room to discover authority of her own.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Davos Seaworth: A former smuggler raised to knighthood by Stannis. Gratitude makes him loyal enough to give his king advice nobody more polished dares to offer.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Samwell Tarly: A book-loving member of the Night's Watch whose father taught him to call himself a coward. Careful reading and concern for others are practical gifts beyond the Wall.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Bran Stark: A boy who loves climbing the walls of Winterfell and imagining himself a knight. His connection to his direwolf grows harder to explain.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Robb Stark: The eldest Stark son has learned to command beside his father. When adults look to him for decisions, the distance between boy and lord shrinks abruptly.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Walder Frey: The elderly lord who controls a crucial river crossing has a vast family and a precise memory for disrespect. Guests negotiate on his ground.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Roose Bolton: A northern lord whose quiet voice makes an audience lean closer. He gives little away while calculating which alliance will best preserve his house.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Oberyn Martell: A Dornish prince, fighter and scholar known as the Red Viper. A public visit to King's Landing brings a long-standing family grievance into reach.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Tywin Lannister: The Lannister patriarch understands armies, money and the calculated public insult. He expects his children to serve a family name he alone gets to define.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Ygritte: A free woman from beyond the Wall who finds Jon's assumptions about wildlings as strange as he finds hers. Teasing gives her lessons a memorable edge.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Sandor Clegane: A scarred fighter in royal service who despises the pretty language of knighthood. His bitter candour unsettles children taught to admire men with swords.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Mance Rayder: A former man of the Night's Watch unites quarrelsome free folk through persuasion as much as force. He knows both sides of the Wall from experience.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-storm-of-swords.Petyr Baelish: The master of coin has risen much further than his birth promised. He speaks of old affections as easily as he moves money and information.

book-stephen-king-the-stand.Stu Redman: A taciturn Texan whose resistance to a lethal illness draws government attention. His steadiness becomes valuable to survivors who have little reason to trust strangers.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Frannie Goldsmith: A pregnant young woman forced to consider what bringing a child into the world means after society collapses.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Randall Flagg: A smiling wanderer in boots who collects followers by offering order. His easy familiarity can change to menace without warning.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Mother Abagail: An elderly Black woman in Nebraska whose faith draws strangers across the country. The tasks of feeding and sheltering them remain very real to her.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Larry Underwood: A musician on the brink of success when the plague hits. Responsibility to other survivors puts pressure on his habit of looking out for himself.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Nick Andros: A deaf, non-speaking drifter whose careful observations and written exchanges make him a natural leader among the scattered survivors.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Tom Cullen: A generous man with an intellectual disability who befriends Nick. His distinctive way of speaking accompanies real courage and a gift for loyalty.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Harold Lauder: A bright, isolated teenager who wants others to notice what he contributes. He keeps a private account of every slight they do notice.
book-stephen-king-the-stand.Nadine Cross: A former teacher drawn to an alarming figure in her dreams. Her tenderness toward a child complicates the future she believes awaits her.

book-victor-hugo-les-miserables.Jean Valjean: A former convict encounters a mercy he cannot fit into his understanding of the world. Keeping faith with that gift costs him successive identities and hard-won security.
book-victor-hugo-les-miserables.Javert: A police inspector sees law, duty and virtue as inseparable. A fugitive who acts generously presents him with a problem no regulation can solve.
book-victor-hugo-les-miserables.Fantine: A young working mother pays others to keep her daughter while concealing the child's existence from employers. Each demand for money reduces her choices.
book-victor-hugo-les-miserables.Cosette: Fantine's daughter grows from a mistreated child into a young woman deeply loved by her guardian. Emerging independence tests a household founded on concealment.
book-victor-hugo-les-miserables.Marius Pontmercy: A young Parisian caught between family histories and political loyalties. Love for Cosette draws him out of abstraction and into decisions with immediate consequences.
book-victor-hugo-les-miserables.Éponine: The Thénardiers' daughter knows the streets, their dangers and the young man who scarcely sees her. Her courage rarely wins the recognition it deserves.
book-victor-hugo-les-miserables.Thénardier: An innkeeper and opportunist treats his household as a business and other people's distress as a chance to collect. Reinvention is one of his durable skills.

book-ken-follett-the-pillars-of-the-eart.Prior Philip: A devout monk who becomes prior of Kingsbridge. His talent for administration and belief in a cathedral draw him into politics far beyond the cloister.
book-ken-follett-the-pillars-of-the-eart.Tom Builder: A master mason who dreams of building a cathedral. He sees structures in terms of load, light and labour while his family faces immediate hunger.
book-ken-follett-the-pillars-of-the-eart.Jack Jackson: A gifted boy raised in the forest who discovers an affinity for carving stone. Craft gives his unconventional intelligence a language other people can recognize.
book-ken-follett-the-pillars-of-the-eart.Aliena: An earl's daughter stripped of the security of rank. Her commercial ingenuity and a promise to her father help her build another life.
book-ken-follett-the-pillars-of-the-eart.William Hamleigh: A brutal young nobleman who treats land, obedience and marriage as entitlements. His family's ambition gives his private cruelty public reach.
book-ken-follett-the-pillars-of-the-eart.Ellen: Jack's mother lives apart from settled society and distrusts church authority. Knowledge that others have buried shapes her response to Kingsbridge.
book-ken-follett-the-pillars-of-the-eart.Waleran Bigod: An ambitious churchman who uses patronage and private information with equal skill. Philip's idealism presents both an opportunity and an obstacle.

book-holly-jackson-good-girl-bad-blood.Pippa Fitz-Amobi: Pip swore off investigations after turning her first case into a podcast. When a friend's brother goes missing, she knows both what publicity can do and what it can cost.
book-holly-jackson-good-girl-bad-blood.Ravi Singh: The accused boy's younger brother has lived for years with his town's verdict. He brings personal knowledge and a dry wit to Pip's investigation.
book-holly-jackson-good-girl-bad-blood.Connor Reynolds: Pip's friend turns to her when his older brother disappears. His certainty that Jamie needs help persists after other people dismiss his fears.
book-holly-jackson-good-girl-bad-blood.Jamie Reynolds: Connor's missing older brother has struggled to find his footing. His family's picture of him leaves parts of his life unexpectedly unexplained.
book-holly-jackson-good-girl-bad-blood.Arthur Reynolds: The Reynolds brothers' father has firm expectations of his older son. He is reluctant to treat Jamie's absence as evidence of danger.
book-holly-jackson-good-girl-bad-blood.Charlie Green: A newer arrival in town whose friendly manner makes conversation easy. Pip's investigation draws neighbours with very different histories into the same orbit.
book-holly-jackson-good-girl-bad-blood.Stanley Forbes: A contributor to the local newspaper whose earlier coverage affected the Singhs. He has reasons to care intensely about what the town believes.

book-emma-donoghue-room.Jack: A five-year-old narrator who understands the whole world through the objects in one room. His exuberant logic makes familiar words mean startlingly specific things.
book-emma-donoghue-room.Ma: Jack's mother creates lessons, games and routines inside captivity. Preserving his sense of safety means choosing very carefully which truths he can understand.
book-emma-donoghue-room.Old Nick: The man controlling the door, the supplies and the rules of the room. Jack encounters his power chiefly through sounds and his mother's precautions.
book-emma-donoghue-room.Grandma: Ma's mother has spent years imagining a reunion. Loving the daughter she remembers and getting to know Jack require different kinds of patience.

book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Jake Brigance: A small-town Mississippi lawyer defending a Black father in a racially charged murder trial. Determination has to carry him past very real fear for his family.
book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Carl Lee Hailey: Tonya's father faces trial after shooting the men who assaulted her. He has already decided whom he trusts to speak for him in court.
book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Ellen Roark: A resourceful law student volunteers on Jake's defence team. Her politics and access to money make her an unlikely fit in his Mississippi practice.
book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Lucien Wilbanks: A disbarred lawyer and Jake's mentor brings a deep knowledge of the county to a case that respectable colleagues would rather avoid.
book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Ozzie Walls: The county's Black sheriff has to keep order while the trial draws armed outsiders and puts his own community under scrutiny.
book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Rufus Buckley: An ambitious district attorney knows a televised prosecution could launch a political career. He plays to a wider audience than the jury.
book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Tonya Hailey: Carl Lee's young daughter survives a brutal assault. Behind the courtroom arguments is a child whose needs are immediate and largely private.
book-john-grisham-a-time-to-kill.Harry Rex Vonner: A hard-nosed divorce lawyer and Jake's friend. He offers practical help without expecting the case to turn the county into a fair-minded place.

book-barbara-kingsolver-the-poisonwood-b.Orleanna Price: The missionary's wife remembers bringing four daughters to the Congo. Guilt sharpens her attention to choices she once regarded as obedience.
book-barbara-kingsolver-the-poisonwood-b.Nathan Price: A Baptist missionary certain his faith can be transplanted intact. He treats correction about local language or crops as a challenge to his authority.
book-barbara-kingsolver-the-poisonwood-b.Rachel Price: The eldest Price daughter misses American comforts and mangles unfamiliar words. Her instinct for self-preservation gives her account a distinctly different cadence.
book-barbara-kingsolver-the-poisonwood-b.Leah Price: A teenager initially devoted to her father who wants to prove herself with a bow. Learning from Congolese neighbours changes where she places her allegiance.
book-barbara-kingsolver-the-poisonwood-b.Adah Price: Leah's twin walks with difficulty and thinks in palindromes and verbal reversals. People who overlook her seldom realize how closely she observes them.
book-barbara-kingsolver-the-poisonwood-b.Ruth May Price: The youngest Price daughter makes friends through play. She interprets politics, illness and adult warnings with a child's startlingly literal logic.
book-barbara-kingsolver-the-poisonwood-b.Anatole Ngemba: A Congolese teacher and interpreter who understands what Nathan's preaching sounds like to his neighbours. His conversations give Leah a political education.

book-jane-austen-persuasion.Anne Elliot: A capable woman overlooked by her family meets the naval officer she once refused. Listening well has taught her a great deal, but speaking plainly will take courage.
book-jane-austen-persuasion.Frederick Wentworth: A naval captain returning with money, distinction and an unhealed sense of rejection. His actions around Anne often speak more generously than his conversation.
book-jane-austen-persuasion.Sir Walter Elliot: Anne's widowed father measures the world by looks and entries in the baronetage. Economy strikes him as a more painful prospect than debt.
book-jane-austen-persuasion.William Elliot: The heir presumptive to Sir Walter's title re-enters the family circle with excellent manners. Anne wonders why he is suddenly so eager to please.
book-jane-austen-persuasion.Louisa Musgrove: A lively young neighbour who likes the idea of being firm in her decisions. Wentworth's praise encourages her to make firmness a matter of pride.
book-jane-austen-persuasion.Lady Russell: Anne's older friend once advised against the engagement from sincere concern. Affection and good judgment do not reliably lead her to the same conclusion.

book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Kaz Brekker: A teenage gang leader who walks with a cane and charges for favours. His plans allow for almost everything except having to admit he needs somebody.
book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Inej Ghafa: An acrobat turned spy who moves across Ketterdam's rooftops in near silence. Her blades bear saints' names, and her faith shapes what jobs she will take.
book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Jesper Fahey: A sharpshooter who can hit almost anything and finds it nearly impossible to leave a gambling table. His jokes speed up when the odds turn ugly.
book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Nina Zenik: A Grisha Heartrender with a gift for languages, a taste for waffles and an inconvenient capacity to care for somebody raised to hate her.
book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Matthias Helvar: A Fjerdan soldier trained to hunt Grisha. His rigid sense of honour becomes painful when his own experience contradicts what he was taught.
book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Wylan Van Eck: A merchant's son with a musician's ear and a knack for explosives. Kaz's crew keeps discovering things his powerful father failed to value.
book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Jan Van Eck: A prosperous merchant who puts contracts, reputation and return on investment above almost everything. He brings the same accounting to his relationship with his son.
book-leigh-bardugo-crooked-kingdom.Pekka Rollins: A Ketterdam crime boss with respectable businesses and a talent for confidence tricks. He has ruined enough lives to have forgotten some of his enemies.

book-rebecca-ross-divine-rivals.Iris Winnow: A young journalist competes for a columnist's job while her brother is away at war. In letters to him, her professional composure gives way.
book-rebecca-ross-divine-rivals.Roman Kitt: Iris's impeccably prepared rival at the newspaper. On the page he can risk a tenderness his formidable family would never encourage in person.
book-rebecca-ross-divine-rivals.Forest Winnow: Iris's older brother leaves home to fight for the goddess Enva. His absence changes the practical details of his sister's life as much as her politics.
book-rebecca-ross-divine-rivals.Attie: A fellow war correspondent who takes Iris under her wing. She brings camaraderie and an athlete's endurance to an assignment far from the newsroom.
book-rebecca-ross-divine-rivals.Marisol: The woman who opens her home to the correspondents near the front. For her, news of the war includes the fate of the woman she loves.

book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Cersei Lannister: A queen regent trying to govern in her son's name, Cersei hears danger in advice as readily as in an open threat. She measures herself against her father's reputation.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Jaime Lannister: A gifted knight known chiefly for killing the king he swore to guard. His insolence makes an effective shield against other people's certainty about his motives.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Brienne of Tarth: A physically powerful swordswoman mocked for wanting to live by a knight's vows. An act of courtesy from Renly has earned him her devotion.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Samwell Tarly: A book-loving member of the Night's Watch whose father taught him to call himself a coward. Careful reading and concern for others are practical gifts beyond the Wall.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Arya Stark: A lord's daughter who would rather learn swordplay than needlework. She pays more attention to servants, animals and escapes than her elders realize.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Sansa Stark: Arya's older sister loves songs of gallant knights and knows how a lady should behave. At court, courtesy acquires uses her songs never taught her.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Arianne Martell: The heir to Dorne suspects her father is denying her the place Dornish law promises. Her ability to win personal loyalty encourages her to take a political risk.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Asha Greyjoy: Balon Greyjoy's seafaring daughter commands a ship and has earned the loyalty of its crew. The succession tests whether the islands will accept that authority ashore.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Victarion Greyjoy: A formidable Iron Fleet commander most comfortable when a problem can be solved by force. His brothers' religious and political ambitions give him less certain footing.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Aeron Greyjoy: A priest of the Drowned God whose uncompromising faith shapes the ironborn succession. His dread of one brother runs deeper than a political disagreement.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Areo Hotah: Captain of Doran Martell's guards, trained to watch, obey and handle a longaxe. Quiet attention gives him a close view of a divided ruling family.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Arys Oakheart: A Kingsguard knight in Dorne whose attachment to Arianne strains his vows. He has thought about honour for years without preparing for this particular choice.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Euron Greyjoy: A well-travelled Greyjoy captain with a dangerous reputation and a flair for promises of impossible conquest. His silences can be as unsettling as his speeches.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Doran Martell: The Prince of Dorne lives with painful gout and a reputation for endless caution. Even his children do not know everything that patience conceals.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Margaery Tyrell: A young queen adept at appearing generous in public. Her close circle of female relatives gives her a kind of social power Cersei finds particularly threatening.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.Petyr Baelish: The master of coin has risen much further than his birth promised. He speaks of old affections as easily as he moves money and information.
book-george-r-r-martin-a-feast-for-crows.The High Sparrow: A religious leader with the bearing of a poor pilgrim. His followers give him leverage over a crown that mistakes humility for political weakness.

book-rachel-gillig-one-dark-window.Elspeth Spindle: A young woman sharing her mind with a monster. She has spent years hiding both the infection that marked her and the voice that answers her thoughts.
book-rachel-gillig-one-dark-window.Ravyn Yew: The captain of the king's Destriers outwardly serves the law that threatens people like Elspeth. His private search for Providence Cards requires an unlikely ally.
book-rachel-gillig-one-dark-window.The Nightmare: An ancient presence in Elspeth's mind, by turns protector, storyteller and unsettling guest. It has its own ideas about the price of lending her strength.
book-rachel-gillig-one-dark-window.Elm Rowan: The king's younger son uses irreverence to survive his brother's court. He knows from experience what a Providence Card can make someone do.
book-rachel-gillig-one-dark-window.Hauth Rowan: The crown prince thinks acquiring a rare Providence Card gives him a claim on its owner as well. Courtesy does little to conceal his entitlement.
book-rachel-gillig-one-dark-window.Ione Hawthorn: Elspeth's cousin is drawn into a royal betrothal through the Maiden Card. Its promise of perfect beauty comes with a frightening change in how she feels.

book-taylor-jenkins-reid-one-true-loves.Emma Blair: A woman who rebuilt her life after her husband's disappearance must face him again. The person returning to him is older than the wife he remembers.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-one-true-loves.Jesse Lerner: Emma's adventurous first husband survives years away from home. To him their marriage still feels immediate, while everybody else's life has moved on.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-one-true-loves.Sam Kemper: A musician who knew Emma growing up and became her partner after Jesse disappeared. His gentleness has to coexist with fear of losing their future.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-one-true-loves.Marie: Emma's older sister stayed close to the family bookstore. Their long history of comparison gives way to a more useful kind of frankness in adulthood.

book-taylor-jenkins-reid-carrie-soto-is-.Carrie Soto: A retired tennis champion comes back to defend her record. She studies an opponent's weakest shot with the same intensity other people reserve for a love letter.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-carrie-soto-is-.Javier Soto: Carrie's father and longtime coach built her game stroke by stroke. His pride in the champion can make it hard to tell when the daughter needs him.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-carrie-soto-is-.Nicki Chan: An elite tennis player approaching Carrie's record. She enjoys her power on court and has little interest in making a former champion's return comfortable.
book-taylor-jenkins-reid-carrie-soto-is-.Bowe Huntley: An aging professional player who agrees to train with Carrie. He knows how it feels to hear the crowd discussing your best years in the past tense.

book-ali-hazelwood-bride.Misery Lark: A Vampyre raised among humans as political collateral. She enters a marriage alliance with a Were carrying a private agenda and a notably dry sense of humour.
book-ali-hazelwood-bride.Lowe Moreland: The Were Alpha agrees to a political marriage for his pack. His formidable public presence sits oddly alongside his patience with his young sister.
book-ali-hazelwood-bride.Serena Paris: A journalist and Misery's closest friend since childhood. A gap in their usually dependable contact sets Misery on the trail of her disappearance.
book-ali-hazelwood-bride.Ana Moreland: Lowe's young sister meets Misery with a child's curiosity, sidestepping assumptions that keep the adult Weres and Vampyres apart.
book-ali-hazelwood-bride.Owen Lark: Misery's twin brother understands their father's political calculations. His more comfortable place in Vampyre society gives the siblings different vantage points on the same family.

book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-kicked-t.Lisbeth Salander: A freelance investigator and gifted hacker who remembers insults and details with equal precision. She guards her autonomy fiercely after years of official interference.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-kicked-t.Mikael Blomkvist: A journalist facing a professional disgrace accepts a wealthy industrialist's old family mystery. He gets people talking by actually listening to them.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-kicked-t.Annika Giannini: Mikael's sister, a lawyer, undertakes Lisbeth's defence. Gaining the trust of a client with excellent reasons to distrust institutions is part of the work.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-kicked-t.Erika Berger: Mikael's editor, business partner and longtime lover. She has to weigh his investigative instincts against the survival of the magazine they built.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-kicked-t.Peter Teleborian: A psychiatrist whose professional authority shaped Lisbeth's childhood. His confident diagnoses have travelled further through official files than her own account.
book-stieg-larsson-the-girl-who-kicked-t.Evert Gullberg: A veteran of a secret intelligence unit determined to protect its history. Retirement has done little to weaken his habits of surveillance and concealment.

book-daphne-du-maurier-rebecca.The second Mrs. de Winter: A young paid companion marries a wealthy widower and arrives at Manderley feeling like a guest. Her lively imagination works especially hard on her own inadequacies.
book-daphne-du-maurier-rebecca.Maxim de Winter: Manderley's widowed owner can be affectionate in private and abruptly distant at home. His new wife struggles to tell which memories account for the change.
book-daphne-du-maurier-rebecca.Mrs. Danvers: The housekeeper preserves Rebecca's rooms with intimate precision. A polite tour in her company can be more destabilizing than an open confrontation.
book-daphne-du-maurier-rebecca.Jack Favell: Rebecca's cousin brings a jaunty, intrusive familiarity to Manderley. He knows things about the old household its current residents would prefer to keep private.
book-daphne-du-maurier-rebecca.Frank Crawley: The estate manager offers Maxim steady loyalty and his new wife a rare source of ordinary kindness. He chooses his words carefully around Rebecca.
book-daphne-du-maurier-rebecca.Beatrice Lacy: Maxim's outspoken sister makes a new arrival feel welcome almost despite herself. She notices changes at Manderley and seldom disguises her first reaction.

book-agatha-christie-murder-on-the-orien.Hercule Poirot: A Belgian detective proud of his moustache and precise habits. He listens as closely to the arrangement of a passenger's story as to its facts.
book-agatha-christie-murder-on-the-orien.Samuel Ratchett: A wealthy American passenger who tries to hire protection. Money has usually settled problems for him, but Poirot takes an immediate dislike to him.
book-agatha-christie-murder-on-the-orien.Monsieur Bouc: Poirot's old friend is a railway executive who wants a murder on his train resolved. Hospitality and institutional self-interest pull in the same direction.
